## Summary

Add a new "Step 0: Work-item audit gate" to the cleanup skill instructions (`skill/cleanup/SKILL.md`) that invokes the audit skill when the current branch has an associated work-item ID, before any branch operations begin.

## Context

The cleanup skill currently has no awareness of work-item lifecycle. This step gates the cleanup process on a work-item audit: if the branch has an associated work item, the audit skill is invoked first. The existing audit skill (`skill/audit/SKILL.md`) produces structured verdicts (`met`/`unmet`/`partial`) that the agent uses to decide whether to proceed or abort.

This is a SKILL.md-only change — agent behavior instructions, no Python code changes.

## Files to modify

- `skill/cleanup/SKILL.md` (insert new Step 0 before current Step 1)

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A new "Step 0" is added before the existing Step 1 in `skill/cleanup/SKILL.md`
2. Step 0 instructs the agent to: check the `work_item_id` field from the `inspect_current_branch.py` JSON output, invoke the audit skill if an ID is found, and proceed or abort based on audit results
3. The step documents the decision rules: all criteria `met` -> proceed; any `unmet`/`partial` -> abort; no acceptance criteria defined -> abort
4. Existing steps 1-9 remain unchanged in behavior and order
5. Step 0 is skipped when no work-item ID is found (e.g., on `main` or branches without tokens)

## Minimal Implementation

- Insert a new section in SKILL.md before the current "1. Inspect current branch"
- Reference the audit skill (`skill/audit/SKILL.md`) invocation pattern
- Document the decision rule: only proceed if every criterion has verdict `met`
- Document the skip logic when no work-item ID is present in the `inspect_current_branch.py` output

## Note

This task covers the audit gate structure. The status transition (on pass) and abort messaging (on failure) are covered by sibling tasks but may be implemented together since they all modify the same Step 0 section.

## Deliverables

- Updated `skill/cleanup/SKILL.md`
data.title: Add audit gate step to cleanup skill

## Summary

Document in the cleanup skill instructions that when the audit passes (all criteria `met`), the agent should transition the work item to `status=completed, stage=in_review` and add a comment before proceeding with branch cleanup.

## Context

This follows the same transition pattern established by SA-0ML7OP7L40QKWDB1 (implement-flow: mark work-item completed/in_review after merge). Consistency with that pattern ensures downstream processes (triage audit, producer review) work correctly.

## Files to modify

- `skill/cleanup/SKILL.md` (additions to Step 0, after audit pass condition)

## Acceptance Criteria

1. SKILL.md Step 0 includes explicit `wl update <id> --status completed --stage in_review` command to run after audit passes
2. The transition uses the same pattern as the implement-flow (SA-0ML7OP7L40QKWDB1): status=completed, stage=in_review
3. A comment is added to the work item documenting that cleanup audit passed, including branch name context: `wl comment add <id> --comment "Cleanup audit passed on branch <branch-name>. Work item transitioned to in_review." --author <agent-name>`
4. The transition happens after the audit passes but before any branch operations begin (i.e., before Step 1)

## Minimal Implementation

- Add transition instructions to Step 0 in SKILL.md after the audit-pass decision point
- Include the exact `wl update` and `wl comment add` commands the agent should run
- Specify that this must happen before proceeding to Step 1

## Note

This modifies the same Step 0 section as the sibling audit-gate and abort-behavior tasks. The implementer may combine all three into a single commit.

## Deliverables

- Updated `skill/cleanup/SKILL.md` (additions to Step 0)
data.title: Add status transition on audit pass

data.description:
## Summary

Define clear abort messaging in the cleanup skill for when the audit gate fails (criteria `unmet`/`partial`) or when no acceptance criteria are defined on the work item.

## Context

When the audit gate determines that cleanup should not proceed, the agent needs clear instructions on what to output and how to halt. There are two abort scenarios:
1. **Criteria unmet/partial:** The audit skill returns one or more criteria with `unmet` or `partial` verdicts.
2. **No acceptance criteria:** The work item has no acceptance criteria section defined, so the audit cannot verify completion.

Both scenarios result in a hard abort — no branch operations are performed.

## Files to modify

- `skill/cleanup/SKILL.md` (abort behavior in Step 0)

## Acceptance Criteria

1. When any criterion is `unmet` or `partial`, the agent outputs a clear message listing which criteria failed and their verdicts (referencing the audit report)
2. When no acceptance criteria are defined on the work item, the agent outputs a message explaining that the work item cannot be verified and cleanup is aborted
3. After abort, no branch operations are performed (steps 1-9 are all skipped entirely)
4. The abort message suggests next steps (e.g., "Fix the unmet criteria and re-run cleanup" or "Add acceptance criteria to the work item and re-run cleanup")

## Minimal Implementation

- Add abort message templates/examples to Step 0 in SKILL.md
- Document the "no acceptance criteria" abort case as a separate condition
- Document explicitly that the agent must not proceed to any subsequent step after abort
- Include example abort output for both scenarios

## Note

This modifies the same Step 0 section as the sibling audit-gate and status-transition tasks. The implementer may combine all three into a single commit.

## Deliverables

- Updated `skill/cleanup/SKILL.md` (abort behavior in Step 0)

Summary: Implement 'wl ampa config' subcommand providing show (default), set <key> <value>, and reset <key> with validation of keys.

## Acceptance Criteria
- 'wl ampa config' prints each config field, its effective value, and the source (env / persisted / default).
- 'wl ampa config set <key> <value>' persists overrides to scheduler_store.json and validates keys; unknown keys are rejected with a clear error.
- 'wl ampa config reset <key>' removes persisted overrides for that key.
- CLI operations respect local-operator-only constraints (file permissions / user ownership).

## Minimal Implementation
- Add subcommand in ampa/scheduler_cli.py following existing CLI pattern.
- Implement validation using SchedulerConfig fields.
- Persist via helper from Feature 1 and trigger SIGHUP on set/reset.
- Add unit tests for CLI parsing and persistence behavior.

## Deliverables
CLI code, tests, help text, docs update.

Summary: Extend command entries with allowed_hours and allowed_days, store windows in UTC, accept/validate ranges (including cross-midnight), and skip commands outside windows.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Command schema includes allowed_hours (e.g., ['9-10','22-2']) and allowed_days (e.g., ['mon-fri']).
- Scheduler selection logic silently skips commands that are currently outside their window.
- Windows are accepted in local timezone on input, stored in UTC, and displayed in local timezone.
- Tests cover cross-midnight windows and DST boundary cases.

## Minimal Implementation
- Add fields to CommandSpec and SchedulerStore handling in ampa/scheduler.py.
- Implement parser for hour and day ranges and integrate checks into selection loop.
- Add unit tests for parsing and evaluation; integration test for skipping commands outside window.

## Deliverables
code changes, tests, schema doc update (ampa/scheduler_schema.md).

Summary: Add a SIGHUP handler in the scheduler daemon that reloads scheduler_store.json immediately so wl ampa config set takes effect without waiting for the next poll.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Daemon installs a SIGHUP handler which reloads the store and new config atomically.
- CLI set/reset signals the running daemon (using existing PID file if present; otherwise a well-known pidfile).
- Reload does not interrupt in-progress runs (only changes selection criteria).
- Tests simulate SIGHUP and validate reload behavior.

## Minimal Implementation
- Add SIGHUP handler in ampa/daemon.py (or scheduler entrypoint) to call the store reload path.
- Update wl ampa config CLI to locate the scheduler PID (existing pidfile or well-known runtime pidfile).
- Add tests to assert in-memory config updates after SIGHUP.

## Deliverables
daemon signal handler, CLI signal code, tests, docs for operator flow.
data.title: Immediate reload via SIGHUP

## Acceptance Criteria
- wl ampa status includes a 'Config (effective)' section showing values and sources.
- If per-command windows are present, status shows summary counts (e.g., '3 commands with windows; 1 currently out-of-window').
- Output formatting matches existing status layout and is readable on typical terminal widths.

## Minimal Implementation
- Add a formatter in ampa/daemon.py or ampa/scheduler_cli.py reusing the loader to produce the effective config view.
- Add tests to assert presence and format of the new section.

## Deliverables
code changes, tests, docs update.

## Summary

The repo-root AGENTS.md references skills via relative paths (e.g. [intakeall skill](skill/intakeall/SKILL.md)). The working tree contains an uncommitted edit rewriting these to absolute paths under /home/rgardler/.pi/agent/skills/, matching how the agent framework resolves skill docs.

## User story

As an agent operator, I want AGENTS.md skill references to use absolute paths so they resolve consistently regardless of the working directory.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] AGENTS.md skill references use absolute /home/rgardler/.pi/agent/skills/ paths
- [ ] No remaining relative skill/ references in AGENTS.md
- [ ] AGENTS.md changes committed to dev with a work item reference
- [ ] critical.mjs tests still pass

data.description:
# Intake Brief: Plan/intake skills iterate over children & verify AC coverage

## Problem statement

When the `plan` or `intake` skills run on a work item that has child work items,
they currently process only the target item — they never descend into the
children. This leaves parent/child AC coverage unverified: a parent's acceptance
criteria may not be collectively covered by its children's ACs, and children are
never themselves planned/intaked (so the decomposition tree can be incomplete
or inconsistent at depth).

## Users

- **Agents running `/skill:plan`** on an epic or other parent with children —
  need the skill to recurse over the whole tree so every level is planned, and
  to verify that the union of child ACs covers the parent ACs.
- **Agents running `/skill:intake`** on a parent with children — need intake to
  run per child (when children exist) and to verify cross-level AC coverage.
- **Operators** — get decomposition trees whose ACs are guaranteed (or
  explicitly flagged) to cover their parents, with gaps auto-closed where
  resolvable and hard conflicts surfaced instead of silently passing.

Example user stories:

- As an agent planning an epic with children, I want the plan skill to iterate
  the whole subtree (respecting dependency order) so I don't have to invoke
  `/skill:plan` per child manually.
- As an agent planning a parent, I want a final review step that verifies the
  children's ACs collectively cover the parent's ACs, auto-closing gaps it can
  resolve and stopping with a clear report when it cannot, so a `plan_complete`
  stage is only reached when coverage is guaranteed.
- As an operator re-running intake on a decomposed epic, I want intake to verify
  AC coverage across the existing children (and per child when configured) so
  the tree stays coherent.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 (tree iteration — plan):** Running `/skill:plan` on a work item with
  children processes the entire subtree, not just the target: the skill
  iterates children (each child's own plan run, recursing to any depth), in
  dependency order first (`wl dep` edges), then listed order. Verified by a
  test with a multi-level tree (parent → children → grandchildren) asserting
  every node is planned and the processing order respects `wl dep` edges.
- **AC2 (tree iteration — intake):** Running `/skill:intake` on a work item
  with children runs intake per child (recursing the subtree) and also verifies
  AC coverage across existing children. Verified by a test where intake on a
  parent with children runs per child and reports coverage.
- **AC3 (collective coverage):** After processing, for every parent node in the
  tree, the union of its children's acceptance criteria collectively covers the
  parent's acceptance criteria (each parent AC is covered by at least one child
  AC). Verified by a coverage-check test with a parent whose ACs are covered
  by children and a negative test where coverage is missing.
- **AC4 (final review step — auto-close & stop):** The skills' final review
  step closes coverage gaps it can resolve unambiguously (e.g. adding a missing
  child AC that directly maps to an uncovered parent AC), and when a gap or
  conflict cannot be resolved, stops and reports rather than advancing
  (`plan_complete`/`intake_complete` not set; item left `open` with a comment
  describing the conflict). Verified by tests: one where an unambiguous gap is
  auto-closed, one where an unresolvable conflict prevents stage advancement.
- **AC5 (docs & tests):** All related documentation is updated to reflect the
  changes (plan SKILL.md, intake SKILL.md, shared helper docstrings), and the
  full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Worklog API only:** read children via `wl show <id> --children --json`;
  dependency edges via `wl dep list <id> --json`. No direct worklog file edits.
- **No work item for the process itself:** the skills must not create a work
  item to track the iteration itself.
- **Idempotence:** re-running must not create duplicate children or duplicate
  comments; existing children are reused/updated per the existing plan-skill
  idempotence rules.
- **Status lifecycle:** all status transitions go through `StatusLifecycle`
  (intake via `intake.py`, plan via `StatusLifecycle.update_status`); the new
  final review step must leave the item in a valid terminal status (`open`,
  `blocked`, or `completed`) even when it stops on an unresolvable conflict.
- **Conservative auto-closing:** only close gaps that are unambiguous (a child
  AC that clearly maps to an uncovered parent AC). Never invent requirements —
  if intent is unclear, record an Open Question / stop instead.
- **Scope:** affects the `plan` and `intake` skills (SKILL.md workflows) and
  their shared helpers. Must not change audit, implement, or other skills'
  behavior. Must not alter the audit skill's parent-child verdict semantics.

## Existing state

- `skill/plan/SKILL.md` decomposes the target into child feature work items;
  it creates children (Process step 7) and runs six automated review stages on
  the freshly generated feature plan, but never recurses into children and has
  no AC-coverage check across the tree. Its "Automated review on existing
  content" path (skip decision) reviews existing content but still does not
  iterate the tree.
- `skill/intake/SKILL.md` prepares a single work item (claim → gather → draft →
  five mini-reviews → find-related → finish). It has no child iteration or
  coverage verification.
- `skill/plan/plan_helpers.py` provides shared autoplan/approval-gate logic;
  it has no tree/coverage helpers.
- `wl` supports `wl show <id> --children --json` and `wl dep list/add/rm`, so
  tree traversal and ordering data are available without new CLI work.
- The audit skill already has parent/child awareness (child stage checks,
  inherited passes) — a useful reference for tree semantics but NOT to be
  modified by this item.

## Desired change

- **Shared helper (new or extended):** a module (e.g.
  `skill/shared/tree_coverage.py` or new functions in `plan_helpers.py`) that:
  1. Fetches the full descendant tree via `wl show <id> --children --json`.
  2. Orders siblings by `wl dep` edges (topological) then listed order.
  3. Extracts ACs from each item's description (`## Acceptance Criteria`
     section).
  4. Computes coverage: for each parent AC, whether any child AC covers it.
  5. Auto-closes unambiguous gaps; returns an explicit list of unresolvable
     conflicts.
- **Plan skill:** add a "tree iteration" step (before/around Process step 7)
  that recurses into children; add a final "AC coverage review" step after the
  six review stages that applies the helper, auto-closes gaps, and on
  unresolvable conflicts stops without advancing the stage (leaving the item
  `open` with a conflict comment).
- **Intake skill:** add a per-child intake pass (when children exist) and a
  final AC-coverage verification step mirroring the plan behavior.
- **Tests:** unit tests for the shared helper (tree fetch/order, AC extraction,
  coverage computation, gap auto-close, conflict detection) plus skill-workflow
  tests asserting stage advancement is blocked on unresolvable conflicts.

## Key Files

- `skill/plan/SKILL.md` — Add tree-iteration and final AC-coverage review steps
  to the Process section.
- `skill/intake/SKILL.md` — Add per-child intake pass and AC-coverage
  verification step.
- `skill/shared/tree_coverage.py` (new) — Shared tree traversal, ordering,
  AC extraction, coverage computation, gap auto-close, conflict detection
  (or equivalent functions added to `skill/plan/plan_helpers.py` if shared
  placement is not preferred).
- `skill/plan/tests/test_plan_helpers.py` — Extend with tree/coverage helper
  tests (or add `skill/shared/tests/test_tree_coverage.py`).
- `skill/intake/tests/` — Workflow tests for per-child intake and coverage
  stop/advance behavior.

## Related work

- `SA-0MRW0G0XZ009TU6E` — Audit runner circular dependency fix; documents the
  audit skill's child-stage semantics (children in `in_review` don't block
  parent closure). Reference only; not to be modified here.
- `SA-0MSK9IOEF007PP5S` — Audit skill: reduce wall-clock time; example of a
  parent item decomposed into children via the plan skill.
- `SA-0MSJI53RX006E2PS` — Reduce initial LLM context; an epic with 6 children,
  useful as a real-world tree for manual validation of the new iteration.
- `skill/implement/SKILL.md` — Already has child-aware logic (recursive child
  implementations, terminal-stage checks); a pattern reference for how skills
  handle trees.
- `skill/audit/SKILL.md` + `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — Parent/child
  verdict and stage semantics; reference for tree behavior conventions.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk: recursion depth/time.** Deep trees could make plan/intake slow or
  loop. Mitigation: recursion bounded by the actual tree; each child processed
  once; idempotent re-runs. Note: no explicit depth cap is assumed unless
  needed — flag in implementation if cycles are possible in worklog trees.
- **Risk: AC extraction brittleness.** Descriptions vary in formatting; ACs may
  be missing or malformed. Mitigation: tolerant extraction; missing ACs treated
  as an uncovered gap reported to the user rather than silently ignored.
- **Risk: auto-closing gaps could invent content.** Mitigation: only
  unambiguous, directly-mapped gaps are auto-closed; everything else stops with
  a report (per AC4).
- **Assumption:** worklog trees are acyclic (a work item's children cannot
  contain it). If a cycle is ever detected, the skill stops and reports.
- **Assumption:** `wl dep list <id> --json` output shape is stable; the helper
  parses both object and array JSON shapes (per existing plan skill guidance).
- **Scope-creep note:** any additional "verify child ACs against parent at
  audit time" ideas are out of scope for this item (audit behavior unchanged)
  and would be tracked as separate work items.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Should the iteration recurse through the entire tree (a parent with
  children whose children also have children — plan/intake each level), or just
  one level of direct children?" — Answer (user): "entire tree". Final: entire
  tree, any depth.
- Q2: "Does 'run the skill on each dependently' mean respecting the `wl dep`
  dependency edges (topological order — an item only after its prerequisites)?
  Or just sequential order as listed?" — Answer (user): "respect dependencies,
  then order listed". Final: topological order by `wl dep` edges, ties broken
  by listed order.
- Q3: "When the final review finds parent ACs not covered by child ACs, should
  the skill block completion (refuse to advance to `plan_complete`/`intake_complete`
  until fixed or explicitly waived), or report the gaps and continue?" — Answer
  (user): "it should close the gaps. If there is conflict that cannot be
  resolved then stop and report, refusing to advance". Final: auto-close
  unambiguous gaps; unresolvable conflicts stop the skill, item left `open`
  with a report comment, stage not advanced.
- Q4: "When intake runs on a parent with children (e.g. re-running on a
  decomposed epic), should it: (a) run intake per child, (b) only verify AC
  coverage across existing children, or (c) both?" — Answer (user): "both".
  Final: intake runs per child AND verifies coverage across existing children.

# 24h experiment: AGENTS.md STE100 instruction — session length & token use vs previous period

## Problem statement

We want empirical evidence on whether instructing agents to "Always use ASD-STE100 Simplified Technical English" changes agent efficiency. Currently unmeasured. This work item runs a controlled 24-hour experiment: add the instruction to the global AGENTS.md, measure session length and token usage per session over the 24h window, compare against the previous 24h window, then revert.

## Users

- **Operator (Ralph)** — wants to know whether an STE-style output constraint affects session duration and token consumption (cost proxy) before deciding whether to adopt it permanently.

User story:
- As an operator, I want a before/after comparison of session length and token use so that I can decide whether "Always use ASD-STE100 Simplified Technical English." in AGENTS.md is worth keeping.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Treatment applied and verified:** `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` (symlinked to `~/.pi/agent/AGENTS.md`) contains exactly the sentence "Always use ASD-STE100 Simplified Technical English." during the experiment window, and is reverted after the window. Both states verified via `grep` (before, during, after).
2. **Baseline metrics computed:** for the 24h period immediately preceding the experiment start (T0), computed from session logs for **all projects**: session count, mean/median session length (minutes), mean/median total tokens per session, input/output/cache breakdown, total tokens, and total cost where recorded.
3. **Experiment metrics computed:** same metrics for the window [T0, T0+24h), sessions attributed to the window by session start timestamp.
4. **Comparison report produced and committed:** delta % and direction for each metric (duration, total tokens, input tokens, output tokens), notable outliers (e.g. sessions with output-token-limit errors), project and model breakdown, and a one-line interpretation per metric. Report lives in the repo (e.g. `docs/experiments/ste100-24h/report.md`).
5. **Reproducible measurement:** a single command re-runs the full analysis over the session-log directory and produces identical results (deterministic). If the measurement is delegated to the proxy's usage tooling, verify that tooling actually exists and runs; otherwise the analysis script in this repo is the source of truth (validated during intake: session logs contain per-message `usage` with input/output/cacheRead/cacheWrite/totalTokens/cost).
6. **All related documentation is updated** to reflect the changes (README/wiki entries, code comments in the analysis script).
7. **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes** (including any tests added for the analysis script).

## Constraints

- **Bare sentence only** — the literal instruction "Always use ASD-STE100 Simplified Technical English." No rule expansion, no dictionary, no enforcement tooling.
- **Global scope** — the change lands in `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` (affects every project). This is intended; the change MUST be reverted after the window.
- **Do not modify** session logs, proxy configuration, or any other project's files.
- **Measurement scope:** all sessions across all projects (per operator decision).
- STE *compliance* measurement (whether outputs actually follow STE) is **out of scope** — this experiment measures only session length and token use. Any compliance sampling should be a separate work item (scope-creep guard).
- Changes to `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` follow the repo's normal workflow: implemented in a worktree, committed to `dev` (never `main`), even though this is a temporary experiment. The symlink `~/.pi/agent/AGENTS.md → AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` means no install step is needed; the instruction takes effect for sessions *started after* the change lands.

## Existing state

- `~/.pi/agent/AGENTS.md` is a symlink to `/home/rgardler/projects/SorraAgents/AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` (verified).
- Session logs at `~/.pi/agent/sessions/<project-slug>/*.jsonl` contain: a `session` header event (start timestamp, cwd, id) and per-message assistant events with a `usage` object (`input`, `output`, `cacheRead`, `cacheWrite`, `totalTokens`, `cost`). Last event timestamp ≈ session end. Verified during intake.
- Baseline sample (SorraAgents sessions only, 2026-08-09): 69 sessions, ~30.5h total, avg 26.6 min/session, avg 3.8M total tokens/session (dominated by cache reads; total-token values include cache). One extreme outlier session (153 min, 146.9M total tokens) associated with repeated output-token-limit errors — the report must handle such outliers (report both mean and median).
- `skill/proxy-usage-analysis/` exists but currently contains **no source files** (only `__pycache__`). If this is the "existing usage skill in the proxy" intended for measurement, it must be verified to actually run; otherwise the analysis script in this work item is authoritative.
- `skill/context-audit/scripts/measure_context.py` measures startup-context bytes — related (our change grows startup context by ~50 bytes) but does not measure session token usage. Run before/after to confirm the addition stays within `docs/dev/context-budget.thresholds.json` if that gate is enforced.

## Desired change

1. Add the sentence to `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` in the worktree; commit to `dev`; record exact commit hash and wall-clock T0.
2. Let the experiment run 24h (T0 → T0+24h). No special agent behavior needed during the window beyond normal work.
3. At T0+24h: collect metrics for [T0−24h, T0) and [T0, T0+24h) across all projects; produce the comparison report; revert the AGENTS_GLOBAL.md change (new commit to `dev`); record revert hash.
4. Deliver: report (metrics table, deltas, outliers, interpretation), AC verification, session-log of the experiment itself.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` — add then revert the STE sentence (the treatment).
- `docs/experiments/ste100-24h/report.md` — comparison report (new).
- `skill/ste100-experiment/scripts/analyze_sessions.py` (new, or revived `skill/proxy-usage-analysis/`) — deterministic analysis over `~/.pi/agent/sessions/**/*.jsonl`; produces per-session duration/tokens and window aggregates + tests.
- `skill/proxy-usage-analysis/` — verify/revive if the proxy-side usage skill is to be used for measurement.

## Related work

- `SA-0MSJI53RX006E2PS` / `SA-0MSJI50Y9005VECR` — "Reduce initial LLM context…" (completed + in-progress): same file (`AGENTS_GLOBAL.md`), context-budget angle. Our +1 sentence slightly increases startup context; keep within budget.
- `SA-0MSLK72KI006N9KP` (F1) — "Startup-context measurement tooling": produced `skill/context-audit/scripts/measure_context.py`; related measurement tooling, different axis.
- `SA-0MSISKM8F004NW1U` — "Reduce audit skill initial session context size": also touches startup-context surface.
- `skill/proxy-usage-analysis/` — intended measurement tool per operator; source currently missing, verify.
- `SA-0MSI51QTA009WDFO` — "Add session logging instruction to AGENTS.md" (in-progress): same file (`AGENTS_GLOBAL.md`); session-traceability comments are how experiment sessions get identified/attributed.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Null result risk:** a bare STE100 sentence may not change model output measurably (no vocabulary enforcement; model may not deeply know STE rules). A null result is a valid outcome — report it as such rather than extending the experiment.
- **Confounds:** session mix (project, work type, human vs automated, model, token-limit error loops) differs between windows; day-of-week/time-of-day effects. Mitigations: report medians alongside means, break down by project/model, describe composition, keep interpretation descriptive (correlation, not causation).
- **Boundary sessions:** sessions spanning T0 or T0+24h attributed by *start timestamp* (documented rule).
- **Measurement tooling uncertainty:** if the proxy usage skill is non-functional, the repo analysis script (AC 5) is authoritative — do not block on proxy tooling.
- **Left-over instruction:** the sentence must be reverted; AC 1 greps verify both states. Add a calendar/reminder if available to avoid the window overrunning.
- **Scope creep:** STE compliance scoring, dictionary enforcement, or policy changes are separate work items (`discovered-from:SA-0MSMC8KRS00164VD` if created).

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **SA-0MLGALPU80E5HBIJ** – Persist pending prompts to tool-output (completed)
- **SA-0MSI51QTA009WDFO** – Add session logging instruction to AGENTS.md (in-progress)
- **SA-0MM03YIY609CP27Y** – Scheduler Test Button Command (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `.worklog/tmp/intake-draft-ste100-experiment-SA-0MSMC8KRS00164VD.md` — matched: 24h, agent, agents, always, asd (+21 more)
- `.worklog/worktrees/wl-SA-0MSLK7LGA003J0KP-compact-agents-global-md-to-8-kb-f4/skill/audit/SKILL.md` — matched: agent, agents, always, bare, decisions (+13 more)
- `.worklog/worktrees/wl-SA-0MSLK7LGA003J0KP-compact-agents-global-md-to-8-kb-f4/skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — matched: agent, agents, always, bare, decisions (+13 more)

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Which AGENTS.md gets the instruction? (a) Global AGENTS_GLOBAL.md — affects every session in every project, most representative; (b) SorraAgents project AGENTS.md only — contained blast radius." — Answer (user): "1. Global". Source: interactive reply 2026-08-09.
- Q2: "Measurement scope: (a) All sessions across all projects, or (b) only sessions in the project(s) whose AGENTS.md carries the instruction?" — Answer (user): "2. All (existing usage skill in the proxy will measure this)". Source: interactive reply 2026-08-09. Note: intake could not locate a functional proxy usage skill — only `skill/proxy-usage-analysis/` with no source files; AC 5 requires verifying that path or falling back to the repo analysis script.
- Q3: "Instruction fidelity: keep the literal sentence only, or append a short key-rule expansion?" — Answer (user): "3. Bare sentence". Source: interactive reply 2026-08-09.

## Assumptions recorded

- T0 = wall-clock time the AGENTS_GLOBAL.md change lands on `dev` (commit time). Baseline = [T0−24h, T0). Experiment = [T0, T0+24h).
- "Previous period" = the immediately preceding 24h window (not same-weekday-matched). Day-of-week parity noted as a reporting nicety, not a requirement.
- Cost metrics used only where the log records `cost`; primary metric is `totalTokens` with input/output/cache breakdown as secondary.

# Enable the context-budget pre-push gate across all framework projects

## Problem statement

Every project that runs the installed pi framework should block a local `git push`
to `dev` when the pi-session startup context surface regresses beyond a
project-appropriate budget. The original rollout plan (2026-08-10) listed six
non-SorraAgents projects, but the framework tooling has since landed and the
project landscape has changed; this intake refreshes the brief to the actual
2026-09-27 state and pins the remaining work.

## Users

- **Framework maintainers** — want a context regression caught locally, before
  it reaches `dev`.
- **Project developers** (e.g. AI_Hell contributors) — should not have to
  remember to run the gate manually.

Example user stories:

- As a framework maintainer, I want every framework project to run the
  context-budget gate on push, so that a skills/AGENTS.md regression cannot
  silently raise session cost across projects.
- As an AI_Hell developer, I want the same pre-push protection as SorraAgents,
  so that my project's startup context does not drift unnoticed.

## Current state (verified 2026-09-27)

The original brief's premises are **stale**. The following already landed
(SorraAgents git history):

| Commit | Item | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `6fbc38cf` | SA-0MT1WMPKZ008DL7S | global-symlink fallback for `measure_context.py` in `.githooks/pre-push` |
| `eca4ae60` | SA-0MT1WNWP2007KU7U / SA-0MT1WO815009KXUC | `--generate-thresholds` / `--write-thresholds` in `measure_context.py` |
| `6052e69c` | SA-0MT1WTF170058NJ7 / SA-0MT1WUEIT006U1HC | `install_pi.sh` wires the v2 hook + `core.hooksPath` |
| `3ca016bd` | SA-0MT1WURSU009NAXS | rollout docs in `docs/dev/context-budget.md` |
| `ddc6f6f5` | SA-0MT1WOWAO000T2P1 | hook passes `--repo-root` (global-symlink correctness) |

Project wiring (verified directly):

| Project | hook | `core.hooksPath` | thresholds | In scope? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| SorraAgents | v3 (gate + sync + test gate) | `.git/hooks` | yes (15,473 B) | canonical |
| ContextHub | v2 | `.githooks` | yes (1,894 B) | yes |
| dev-scripts | v2 | `.githooks` | yes (371 B) | yes |
| llm-manager | v2 | `.githooks` | yes (967 B) | yes |
| open_source_llm | v2 | `.githooks` | yes (2,048 B) | yes |
| Tableau-Card-Engine | v2 | `.githooks` | yes (46,807 B) | yes |
| AI_Hell | **v1 (sync only)** | **unset** | **none** (project AGENTS.md = 24,044 B) | **yes — ungated** |
| ampa | v1 (sync only) | unset | none | **no — retired 2026-08-20** per `docs/dev/context-budget.md` L215 |

Notes:

- `docs/dev/context-budget.md` (§ Rollout to all framework projects) states
  ampa was retired on 2026-08-20 and is out of scope.
- The brief's claim that "the global `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` is symlinked to all
  projects" is inaccurate: `install_pi.sh` symlinks it to
  `~/.pi/agent/AGENTS.md` (machine-global), not into each repo. Consequently
  `measure_context.py` reports `global_agents = 0` and (mostly)
  `skills_prose = 0` in non-SorraAgents repos; each project's gate protects its
  **repo-local** surface, and the global surface is gated by SorraAgents itself.
- AI_Hell is an active framework project (last commit 2026-09-27) with a v1
  hook and no thresholds — a genuine remaining gap under the item title
  "across all framework projects".

## Target outcome

Every in-scope framework project's push to `dev` runs the context-budget gate
with project-appropriate committed thresholds. The only remaining project is
AI_Hell; the rollout is otherwise complete and should be verified end-to-end
before this item is closed.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: v2 pre-push hook resolves `measure_context.py` from the local repo path
  when present, else the installed global symlink
  (`~/.pi/agent/skills/context-audit/scripts/measure_context.py`), and stays
  fail-open only when the framework is absent entirely. *(met — `tests/test_pre_push_hook_fallback.py`)*
- AC2: A repeatable per-project baseline flow emits a committed thresholds file
  (`docs/dev/context-budget.thresholds.json`) for the project.
  *(met — `measure_context.py --write-thresholds`; `tests/test_measure_context.py`)*
- AC3: The v2 hook + gate + `core.hooksPath` are installed in **every in-scope**
  framework project. *(partial — 5 of 5 listed projects done; **AI_Hell
  outstanding**; ampa retired/out of scope)*
- AC4: Worklog sync behaviour is preserved in every project (no v1→v2
  regression). *(met for wired projects — v2 hook contains the sync block)*
- AC5: `scripts/install_pi.sh` propagates the hook/global tooling so future
  projects get the gate automatically, and docs describe the mechanism.
  *(met — `tests/test_install_pi_hook_wiring.py`; `docs/dev/context-budget.md`)*
- AC6: End-to-end verification: a simulated push in at least one real
  non-SorraAgents framework project fires the gate (blocks an over-budget
  surface, passes a within-budget one). *(unmet — only temp-repo unit tests
  exist; no recorded real-project verification)*
- AC7: All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including
  code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
  *(pending — refresh rollout table with AI_Hell and the corrected
  global/local measurement note)*
- AC8: Full project test suite must pass with the new changes (pytest + Node),
  including `tests/test_context_budget_gate.py`,
  `tests/test_pre_push_hook_fallback.py`, and
  `tests/test_install_pi_hook_wiring.py`. *(pending confirmation)*

## Constraints

- ampa is out of scope (retired 2026-08-20 per `docs/dev/context-budget.md`).
- The gate must remain fail-open when the framework/tooling is absent (old
  worktrees, machines without pi).
- `git config core.hooksPath .githooks` is the repo-level wiring mechanism
  (SorraAgents itself uses `.git/hooks`; do not change that without reason).
- Thresholds are generated from a project's own measurement; no shared global
  threshold value.
- Do not add CI/CD pipeline tests.

1. Run `scripts/install_pi.sh` (or the hook-wiring block) in AI_Hell to install

4. Add or record an end-to-end simulated-push verification for one real

5. Confirm the SorraAgents full suite is green.

- `scripts/install_pi.sh` — already wires hooks; verify it runs cleanly in

- `tests/test_context_budget_gate.py`, `tests/test_pre_push_hook_fallback.py`,

## Summary
run_tests.py (skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py) resolves its target repo from its OWN install location (REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3] = the SorraAgents framework repo), not from the invoking project. The CLI (main -> run_all without cwd -> cwd = cwd or REPO_ROOT) therefore runs/caches the FRAMEWORK repo's suite when invoked from any other project.

## Evidence (from llm repo, cwd=/home/rgardler/projects/llm)
- 'python3 /home/rgardler/.pi/agent/skills/test/scripts/run_tests.py --summary --suite pytest' printed '8 failed, 1814 passed' — that is the SORRAAGENTS suite (llm's suite is 2130 passed, exit 0).
- '--json --suite pytest' returned cached=True returncode=1 — reading the SorraAgents cache, not the llm cache.
- The audit skill compensates correctly: TARGET_PROJECT_ROOT = git rev-parse --show-toplevel at import; passes cwd=str(project_root) to query_cached/run_cached, so the llm cache entries are written/read via the audit path only.

## Impact
An agent or operator following the test skill's documented invocation (python3 ./scripts/run_tests.py --json) from a non-framework project tests and caches the WRONG repo's suite. Cross-project consumers must remember to pass cwd explicitly (audit does; ship/implement pass cwd where relevant).

## Proposed fix (minimal)
Detect the invoking project root from cwd at CLI time — e.g. 'git rev-parse --show-toplevel' from os.getcwd() when --cwd is not passed (mirroring audit_runner.TARGET_PROJECT_ROOT), falling back to REPO_ROOT. Preserve existing behavior when invoked from the framework repo itself. Alternatively add a --project-root flag and document it in the test skill SKILL.md.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] run_tests.py CLI run from a non-framework project (e.g. llm) targets that project's repo + cache (git-state fingerprint at that project's HEAD), not SorraAgents.
- [ ] Invoked from the framework repo itself, behavior is unchanged.
- [ ] Audit skill read-only auto-verification (query_cached at TARGET_PROJECT_ROOT) still hits the same cache entries.
- [ ] Test skill SKILL.md documents the project-root resolution (and any --project-root flag).

On 2026-08-11, a `wl import` into the ContextHub worklog store replaced the entire target database (~2,800 items wiped), requiring a bespoke SQLite free-page recovery script to restore data. This procedure should be documented in the global AGENTS.md (installed to `~/.pi/agent/AGENTS.md` via `install_pi.sh`) so agents and operators know the canonical recovery path and the destructive semantics of `wl import`.

# Replace scan.py find-workitem with native wl CLI lookup in audit prompts

## Problem statement

The audit SCANNING blocks and docs currently recommend
`scan.py find-workitem <id>` for worklog lookups (wired in by
SA-0MSBR0SRK0035HB1; guidance refined by SA-0MSOIS36N0024ORI).
`scan.py find-workitem` wraps `wl search <id> --json` plus an exact-id
post-filter. Once the wl CLI gains tolerant ID resolution (the ContextHub
feature below), audit agents should use native wl commands for worklog
lookups and `scan.py find-workitem` can be retired.

## Blocked by

- **WL-0MSOMI4GQ009WL8E** — "Add tolerant work-item ID resolution to `wl show`
  (exact-first, unique substring fallback, ambiguity error) for agent tool
  use" — feature request in the **ContextHub** repository
  (`/home/rgardler/projects/ContextHub`), created 2026-08-11.

This item MUST NOT start until that feature lands in the installed wl CLI
(the exact-match `wl show` today cannot resolve partial/truncated IDs, which
is why the scan.py wrapper exists). Cross-project dependency — recorded here
as a blocker; not a `wl dep` edge (different worklog DBs).

## Substring-matching guidance (researched — use ONLY the optimal command)

The canonical substring-matching primitive is **`wl list <term> --json`**:
case-insensitive substring match over id/title/description, JSON mode returns
all matches, supports `-n/--number` and filters (see `src/commands/list.ts`
in ContextHub).

`wl search <keywords> --json` is full-text search (FTS, token/prefix-based) —
**not** a substring matcher — and must NOT be presented as one.

Exact / unique-ID resolution: **`wl show <id> --json`** (tolerant once
WL-0MSOMI4GQ009WL8E lands; `scan.py find-workitem <id>` interim).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. All SCANNING blocks in `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`
   (`_PHASE1_SCANNING_BLOCK`, phase2_child, phase2_batch, phase2_deep) direct
   worklog lookups to native wl commands only:
   - substring matching: `wl list <term> --json`
   - exact/unique-ID resolution: `wl show <id> --json`
2. The dual recommendation "`wl search <keywords> --json` or
   `wl list <term> --json` for substring matching" (introduced by
   SA-0MSOIS36N0024ORI) is corrected to the single optimal command
   **`wl list <term> --json`** everywhere it appears (audit_runner.py +
   docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md), per the research note above.
3. `scan.py find-workitem` is removed (subcommand, its tests, and references
   in audit-grep-scan-patterns.md) OR deprecated with a clear notice — the
   decision is documented in a comment; `scan.py search-code` and
   `scan.py list-files` remain unchanged.
4. docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md and docs/dev/audit-grep-scan-patterns.md
   (incl. the P9 replacement recipe) updated to the native commands.
5. Full project test suite passes (canonical PATH with `~/.local/bin`).
6. Related docs (README, wiki/docs-site entries, code comments, scan.py
   module docstring) updated; no stale `scan.py find-workitem` guidance
   remains.

## Out of scope

- No changes to `scan.py search-code` / `list-files` (bounded code search).
- No changes to the wl CLI itself — tracked in ContextHub WL-0MSOMI4GQ009WL8E.
- No changes to audit verdict semantics or prompt structure beyond the
  worklog-lookup guidance lines.

## Related work

- SA-0MSOIS36N0024ORI — removed stale `.worklog/worklog-data.jsonl` grep
  guidance from audit prompts (completed, this item's precursor).
- SA-0MSBR0SRK0035HB1 — wired scan.py guidance into audit prompts (the
  guidance this item replaces).
- SA-0MSAEJCP7002LTIM / SA-0MSBSOAEM0078LAO — scan hygiene parents.

# Problem statement

`pytest` is installed at `~/.local/bin/pytest` (Python 3.14, user site-packages) but `~/.local/bin` is NOT on the PATH in non-login shells (e.g., agent tool shells, nohup/cron contexts). Running `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py --force` from such a shell fails with "command not found: pytest" — the pytest suite is skipped (returncode null), no green pytest cache entry is produced at HEAD, and the audit skill's automatic full-suite verification is degraded ("Automatic full-suite verification unavailable ... execution-dependent criteria stay partial").

# Observed (during audit of SA-0MSMAZP6T007NM0O, 2026-08-12)

- `python3 -c "import pytest"` succeeds: pytest 9.1.1 at /home/rgardler/.local/lib/python3.14/site-packages
- `~/.local/bin/pytest` exists
- Non-login shell: `pytest` → command not found
- Fix on the spot: `export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"` then rerun → suite green (pytest + node, 0 failures)

# Users

- AI agents running `/skill:test` or `run_tests.py` from tool shells
- The audit skill runner, which reads the test cache to auto-verify execution-dependent ACs
- Operators running the test suite from cron/non-login contexts

# Acceptance Criteria

1. `run_tests.py` runs the pytest suite successfully from a non-login shell (no manual `export PATH`) and produces a green cache entry at HEAD.
2. The fix does not break the suite when run from a login shell or when `pytest` is already on PATH (all existing tests still pass).
3. The fix is covered by tests in the test-runner test area (e.g., `tests/test_run_tests_cache.py` / `tests/test_test_runner.py`).
4. Running `/skill:test` (or the canonical runner) from the default agent shell at HEAD yields 0 failures.

# Constraints

- Changes limited to the test runner tooling (`skill/test/scripts/`) and its tests.
- Prefer the simplest robust resolution (e.g., `~/.local/bin` PATH fallback or `python3 -m pytest` fallback) — no speculative rework.
- Do not modify agent-infrastructure dirs outside the test skill.

# Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` — pytest command resolution
- `tests/test_run_tests_cache.py` / `tests/test_test_runner.py` — tests for the fix

# Risks & assumptions

- Risk: hardcoding `~/.local/bin` may not apply to other environments. Mitigation: fall back to PATH lookup first, then `~/.local/bin`, then `python3 -m pytest`.
- Assumption: pytest is the canonical Python test runner for this repo (node suites already resolve fine).

The audit skill's Phase 1 merge gate (_integrate_into_dev in skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py, ~lines 6099-6109) unconditionally runs 'npm run build' after merging the item's work into an integration worktree (build -> test -> commit order per AGENTS.md). For a repo without package.json / build tooling (e.g. docs-only repos such as AI_Hell), this fails with ENOENT and the gate reports 'Merge gate blocked: integration failed: build failed' -> 'Ready to close: No', demoting the item to open/plan_complete — even though the git merge itself succeeded (rc=0) and the change is valid.

User story: As an operator auditing a docs-only work item in a repo without build tooling, I want the audit merge gate to skip/soften the build step so valid changes can pass Phase 1 without the workaround of committing+pushing to dev first.

Impact: any docs-only item in a repo without build tooling cannot pass the audit merge gate when the work is not yet in dev. Workaround (used for AH-0MT7VE4SX0005A8V): commit + push to dev FIRST, then audit — _verify_merged_in_dev detects the work already in origin/dev and fails open without attempting the build.

Steps to reproduce:
1. Have an audited work item whose commits are NOT yet in origin/dev.
2. Run the audit on a repo with no package.json (e.g. a docs-only GDD repo).
3. Observe the Phase 1 merge gate fail with 'build error'/'build failed' despite the merge succeeding.

Suggested fix: make the build step conditional on the integration worktree having package.json (or a configured build command, e.g. .pi/test-config.json buildCommand), or record a non-blocking note when no build tooling exists. Mirror the conditional-skip approach already applied to the implement skill's run_build() (SA-0MSM6JHG9002CZA1) and run_tests() (SA-0MSN4AXIQ007IZG2).

Acceptance criteria:
1. Audit Phase 1 integration succeeds for a repo with no package.json and no build tooling; the build step is skipped and recorded as evidence (non-blocking note), not a failure.
2. Audit Phase 1 still runs 'npm run build' and fails the gate when a package.json with a build script exists and the build fails.
3. Existing merge-gate tests (skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_merge_gate.py and related) remain green; a new test covers the no-build-tooling case.
4. Behavior is consistent with the implement skill's conditional build/test skip conventions (SA-0MSM6JHG9002CZA1, SA-0MSN4AXIQ007IZG2).

## Problem

The audit runner's merge gate (`_resolve_item_integration_evidence`) extracts candidate commit SHAs from work-item descriptions and comments using the regex `\b[0-9a-f]{7,40}\b`. This regex incorrectly matches decimal numbers that happen to be composed entirely of hex digits (e.g., `0.23290948243196963` from a test failure message). The numeric sequence after the decimal point (`2329094824319696`, `231051271500847`) is treated as a valid commit SHA, causing false-positive merge-gate failures.

**Example:** A failing test with the error:
```
expected 0.23290948243196963 to be less than or equal to 0.2310512715008475
```
produces candidate commits `2329094824319696` and `231051271500847` from the audit runner, which then fail to integrate into `dev` because they are not real commit SHAs.

## Root Cause

File: `.pi/skills/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`, function `_resolve_item_integration_evidence`, line ~6119:

```python
for m in re.finditer(r"\b[0-9a-f]{7,40}\b", desc, re.IGNORECASE):
```

The `\b` word boundary does not prevent matching within decimal numbers. The sequence `0.23290948243196963` is parsed as a decimal literal, but the substring `2329094824319696` (16 hex chars) passes the 7-40 char hex check.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Audit no longer extracts decimal numbers as commit SHAs:** The regex in `_resolve_item_integration_evidence` must not match numeric sequences that are part of decimal literals (e.g., `0.23290948243196963` → no SHA extracted; `2329094824319696` → no SHA extracted).

2. **Valid commit SHAs are still extracted:** The fix must not break extraction of legitimate commit SHAs:
   - Full 40-hex SHAs (e.g., `2c15ebd3cc78f415afca198930339f2138bed218`)
   - Short 7-39 hex SHAs (e.g., `2c15ebd`, `abc1234`)
   - SHAs in commit messages, WL comment text, and work-item descriptions

3. **Commit SHAs prefixed by `#` (GitHub-style) are still extracted:** `#2c15ebd` or `sha=2c15ebd` patterns should still be detected (the `\b` boundary handles `#` as a non-word character, so the hex sequence is still matched).

4. **All existing audit tests pass:** No regression in the existing audit test suite (`/home/rgardler/.pi/agent/skills/audit/tests/`).

5. **New test coverage:** Add a test that verifies decimal numbers are not extracted as commit SHAs, and a test that verifies valid SHAs in various formats (full, short, GitHub-style) are still extracted.

## Suggested Fix

Replace the regex `\b[0-9a-f]{7,40}\b` with one that excludes decimal-point-adjacent sequences. Options:

**Option A (negative lookbehind for dot):**
```python
for m in re.finditer(r"(?<!\.)\b[0-9a-f]{7,40}\b(?!\.)", desc, re.IGNORECASE):
```

This uses `(?<!\.)` to ensure the match is not preceded by a decimal point, and `(?!\.)` to ensure it is not followed by one.

**Option B (explicit non-digit-dot context):**
```python
for m in re.finditer(r"(?<![0-9.])\b[0-9a-f]{7,40}\b(?![0-9.])", desc, re.IGNORECASE):
```

This is more aggressive — it excludes any sequence preceded or followed by digits or dots.

**Option C (split on dots first, then match):**
Preprocess the text: `text.replace('.', ' ')`, then apply the original regex. This is simpler but could break SHAs that happen to be adjacent to dots in unusual contexts (unlikely but possible in commit messages).

**Recommended:** Option A — targeted fix that only excludes decimal-point adjacency, preserving all other behavior.

## Impact

- **Scope:** Single function in `audit_runner.py` (`_resolve_item_integration_evidence`)
- **Risk:** Low — the change is a regex refinement; behavior is identical for all real commit SHAs.
- **Test coverage:** Existing audit tests cover SHA extraction from descriptions and comments; add a test for decimal exclusion.

## Related Work

- N/A — this is a bug in the audit skill's core merge-gate logic.
data.title: audit-runner: decimal numbers incorrectly extracted as commit SHAs in merge gate

## Goal

Collect data and make a recommendation on whether the herdr downtime dispatcher's strict idle gate for audit dispatch should be relaxed. This is a research/investigation item — it produces a recommendation, not code changes (unless the recommendation is to change the gate).

## Problem

The herdr idle gate requires >= 60s continuous idle + >= 2 free slots before dispatching ANY work (including audits). This gate is the hard throughput ceiling: even with a bounded queue and batch drain, audits can only run when this gate opens. We need data to decide if relaxing this gate for audit-only dispatch is necessary.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Data collection:** after deploying SA-0MTG5RYH8005RQNM + SA-0MTG5TP5Z008QBL5 (bounded queue + batch drain), collect 7-day metrics on:
   - Gate opening frequency (how many windows per day)
   - Average window duration
   - Items drained per window (with batch drain)
   - Resulting time-to-audit for items in various priority tiers

2. **Analysis:** compute the theoretical throughput under current gate vs. proposed relaxed gate options:
   - Current: gate opens every ~X minutes, N items drained per window
   - Relaxed gate (audit-only, 10s idle OR any idle when slots available): estimated openings per day, throughput

3. **Recommendation with evidence:** a documented recommendation (keep gate / relax for audits / remove gate) with supporting metrics from step 1-2.

4. **Actionable next step:** if recommendation is to change the gate, create a child work item in the herdr ContextHub worklog (or here if in SorraAgents repo scope) with a clear implementation plan.

- Comment on this work item with the analysis and recommendation
- If gate change is recommended: create a follow-up work item with implementation plan

# Integration Tests for Plan/Intake Tree Iteration & Coverage

## Problem statement

The audit of SA-0MSLRVQIF0040GAM found that while the shared helper functions (tree_coverage.py) and SKILL.md workflows are well-tested at the unit level, three acceptance criteria (AC1, AC2, AC4) lack end-to-end integration tests that exercise the actual skill mutation behavior:

- **AC1:** No integration test exercises the full plan skill workflow with a multi-level tree (parent → children → grandchildren) asserting end-to-end processing order respects `wl dep` edges.
- **AC2:** No integration test exercises the full intake skill workflow with per-child intake runs and coverage verification.
- **AC4:** No test exercises the actual skill mutation behavior — adding missing child ACs, setting status=open with conflict comments, and blocking stage advancement on unresolvable conflicts.

## Users

- **Agents** running `/skill:plan` on epics with children — need confidence that the tree iteration processes correctly in a multi-level dependency graph.
- **Agents** running `/skill:intake` on decomposed epics — need confidence that per-child intake and coverage verification work as documented.
- **Operators** — need integration test coverage that validates the full workflow, not just the helper functions in isolation.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 (plan integration):** A test creates a multi-level tree via `wl` commands (parent → 2 children, one child has a grandchild), sets up dependency edges, and runs the plan skill's tree-iteration step (or an equivalent agent-workflow script). The test asserts: every node is processed, the processing order respects `wl dep` edges (topological order with listed-order tie-breaking), and the final stage advancement comment is written.
- **AC2 (intake integration):** A test creates a parent with existing children that have partial AC coverage, runs the intake skill's per-child intake step, and asserts that: each child is processed, coverage is computed across children, and the coverage verification step either auto-closes gaps (when unambiguous) or stops (when conflicts exist).
- **AC3 (mutation behavior — auto-close):** A test simulates an unambiguous coverage gap (parent AC not covered by any child AC, but a clear mapping exists) and asserts that the skill workflow creates/updates a child work item to cover the gap, then advances to `plan_complete`/`intake_complete`.
- **AC4 (mutation behavior — stop on conflict):** A test simulates an unresolvable conflict (parent AC cannot be mapped to any child AC, or mapping would invent requirements) and asserts that: the skill leaves the item in `open` status, writes a comment describing the conflict, and does NOT advance to `plan_complete`/`intake_complete`.
- **AC5 (idempotence):** Re-running the integration test (with the same tree state) does not create duplicate children or duplicate comments, and the final state is identical to the first run.

## Constraints

- Tests must use the Worklog API only (`wl` CLI) — no direct file edits.
- Tests must work against the same worklog backend used in the existing test suite.
- Tests should create and clean up their own work items (ephemeral test tree).
- Must not modify or depend on audit, implement, or other skills' behavior.
- Must not alter the audit skill's parent-child verdict semantics.

## Key Files

- `skill/shared/tests/test_tree_coverage.py` — Extend with integration-level tree workflow tests (or add `skill/shared/tests/test_plan_integration.py` / `skill/shared/tests/test_intake_integration.py` if a separate file is preferred).
- `skill/plan/SKILL.md` — Reference for expected processing order and mutation behavior.
- `skill/intake/SKILL.md` — Reference for expected per-child intake and coverage verification.

## Related work

- Parent: SA-0MSLRVQIF0040GAM — Plan/intake skills: iterate over children, ensure child ACs collectively cover parent ACs (in_review).
- SA-0MRW0G0XZ009TU6E — Audit runner circular dependency fix; reference for tree semantics.

# Audit Stuck in `in_progress` When `run-release` is Aborted

## Problem Statement

When the `run-release` script is aborted (e.g., via Ctrl+C or signal) while the audit gate is running audits on work items, those items are left stuck in the `in_progress` state. The audit runner's `wl update --status in_progress` claim is performed before the try/finally block in `cmd_issue` can catch the abort, and a hard kill (SIGKILL) bypasses Python's finally blocks entirely. This breaks the release pipeline because items stuck in `in_progress` are excluded from the `in_review` candidate query.

## Users

- **Release operator**: Runs `run-release` and needs the pipeline to complete or abort cleanly without manual work-item intervention.
- **Automated agents**: Agents waiting for work items to reach `in_review` stage to proceed with release gating.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Audit runner restores pre-audit status on hard abort**: When the `audit_runner.py` process receives SIGKILL (signal 9) during an audit, it must still restore the work item to its pre-audit state (`completed`/`in_review` or whatever it was before the audit). Since Python cannot catch SIGKILL, the solution must use a subprocess wrapper or a separate watchdog process that observes the audit child's death and restores the captured pre-audit status.
- **AC2 — Audit runner restores status on SIGTERM/SIGINT**: When the `audit_runner.py` process receives SIGTERM or SIGINT, the status restoration must still complete even if killed mid-try-block. Python's default SIGINT handling raises `KeyboardInterrupt`, so the `finally` block in `cmd_issue` covers SIGINT, but the default SIGTERM disposition terminates the process *without* running `finally` blocks. An explicit `SIGTERM`/`SIGINT` handler that performs the cleanup and then re-raises (or restores the default disposition and re-signals) is therefore required for SIGTERM.
- **AC3 — No `in_progress` items left after any abort scenario**: After any termination of `audit_runner.py` (SIGTERM, SIGINT, SIGKILL, or process death), the audited work item must NOT remain in `in_progress` state. This can be verified by checking the work item's status after a forced kill.
- **AC4 — All existing audit tests pass**: The fix must not break any existing audit tests in `skill/audit/tests/`.

## Constraints

- The fix must not introduce new race conditions in concurrent audit scenarios (multiple `audit_runner.py` processes auditing the same or different items).
- The solution must follow existing project conventions: no direct `wl update` outside the audit runner's lifecycle management.
- If a direct Python-level SIGKILL handler is impossible, a wrapper mechanism (e.g., a parent process that monitors the child and cleans up on death) must be used.

## Existing State

- The audit runner (`skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`) sets `in_progress` status in `_phase_gate` (the `wl update ... --status in_progress` claim is issued at `audit_runner.py:8219`; `_phase_gate` starts at line 7938) before entering the main `try/finally` block in `cmd_issue`.
- The `finally` block in `cmd_issue` calls `_apply_terminal_lifecycle` which restores the pre-audit state.
- `check-audit-gate.js` (used by `run-release.js`) invokes `audit_runner.py issue <id>` via `execSync` for each candidate work item.
- When the `run-release` script is aborted, the `execSync` call is terminated, killing the `audit_runner.py` child process.
- If killed with SIGKILL (signal 9), Python's `finally` blocks do not execute, leaving the item in `in_progress`.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — Needs a signal handling mechanism or wrapper to ensure status restoration on hard abort.
- `skill/ship/scripts/check-audit-gate.js` — May need a timeout/abort handler to clean up on termination.
- `skill/audit/tests/` — New tests for abort scenarios.

## Related Work

- **SA-0MSQRZ5N6005WI43**: [test-failure] test-check-audit-gate.mjs / test-close-work-items.mjs / test-run-release.mjs (6 node failures) — failing test (still open, critical priority)
- **SA-0MSBU4OBU005WJNB**: Implement skill: gate implementation on Code Freeze status — uses trap/finally pattern for exit cleanup (relevant pattern to follow)

## Clarifying Questions & Answers

- Q: "Is the abort specifically SIGKILL, or does SIGTERM also fail to restore status?" — Answer (Map): SIGTERM should be handled by Python's finally blocks, but SIGKILL cannot be caught by Python at all. The fix must handle SIGKILL via a wrapper mechanism. Source: interactive reply.
- Q: "Can a wrapper process approach work here?" — Answer (Map): Yes, a parent process that monitors the child and cleans up on death is an acceptable approach. Source: interactive reply.
data.title: Audit stuck in in_progress when run-release is aborted

# Add duplicate-work detection guidance to intake/plan/implement skills

## Problem statement

Agents working on SorraAgents work items sometimes discover that the work they have been asked to do already exists in another item (e.g., the AI_Hell "Player should be a shape that shows direction" item was a duplicate of an already-shipped feature). Currently, there is no explicit guidance in the intake, plan, or implement skills telling agents how to handle such situations — they either waste effort implementing already-done work or leave the duplicate item hanging.

## Users

- **Agents** (Map, implement, etc.) — need clear instructions on what to do when they detect duplicate or overlapping work during intake, planning, or implementation.
- **Operators/producers** — benefit from reduced wasted effort and cleaner backlog with no orphaned duplicate items.

### Example user stories

- As an **agent**, when I discover that the work I was assigned likely already exists in another work item, I want to check for that item and compare acceptance criteria so I don't waste effort re-implementing completed work.
- As an **operator**, I want duplicate work items to be either closed (if the work is fully covered) or rewritten to address only the remaining differences, so my backlog stays clean and actionable.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Intake skill guidance added:** The `skill/intake/SKILL.md` file includes a new section instructing the agent, during Step 2 (Gather context), to search for and identify work items that may represent duplicate or overlapping work. If such an item is found, the agent must: (a) compare the acceptance criteria of the current item against the existing item, (b) if the ACs are fully covered by the existing item, close the current item with reason "Duplicate of <existing-item-id>: work already completed" and record a comment explaining the decision, (c) if there are differences, rewrite the current item's description and ACs to address only those differences and link the existing item as related work.

- [ ] **AC2 — Plan skill guidance added:** The `skill/plan/SKILL.md` file includes equivalent duplicate-detection guidance for the planning phase. If, while decomposing or reviewing children, a child's scope overlaps with an existing completed item, the agent follows the same AC-comparison procedure: close the duplicate or rewrite to cover remaining gaps.

- [ ] **AC3 — Implement skill guidance added:** The `skill/implement/SKILL.md` file includes duplicate-detection guidance. Before beginning implementation (during worktree creation or early review), the agent must verify that the work described in the item has not already been completed in the repository. If a matching completed work item is found, the agent follows the same procedure: compare ACs, close if covered, or rewrite if only partial overlap exists.

- [ ] **AC4 — Decision procedure documented:** A clear, step-by-step decision procedure is documented in all three skills:
  1. Search for potential duplicates using `wl search` (keywords from title/description) and `wl list` (related tags, assignee).
  2. Review the description and acceptance criteria of any candidate duplicate items.
  3. Compare ACs: are all acceptance criteria of the current item fully satisfied by the existing item?
     - **Yes → Close this item.** Record a comment: "Duplicate of <existing-item-id>: all acceptance criteria are met by that item. Closing to avoid redundant work." Then `wl close <id> --reason "Duplicate of <existing-item-id>: work already completed" --json`.
     - **No (partial overlap) → Rewrite this item.** Update the description and ACs to address only the differences/gaps. Record a comment: "Rewritten to address differences from <existing-item-id>: <summary of differences>." Link the existing item as related work.
     - **No (no overlap found) → Proceed normally.** Document that a duplicate check was performed and no overlapping completed item was found.

- [ ] **AC5 — Comment templates provided:** Each skill includes ready-to-use comment templates for the three outcomes (full duplicate, partial overlap rewrite, no overlap found) to ensure consistency and traceability.

- [ ] **AC6 — All existing tests pass** after any changes to the skill files.

## Constraints

- Keep the additions concise — these are guidance sections, not full specs. Aim for ~15-25 lines per skill.
- Do not change any skill script logic (`scripts/` files) — this is documentation-only guidance within SKILL.md files.
- Follow the existing style and structure of each skill file (headings, code blocks, lists).
- The guidance must be idempotent: re-running the check on the same item produces the same result.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/intake/SKILL.md` — Add duplicate-detection section (likely in Step 2 or as a new step).
- `skill/plan/SKILL.md` — Add duplicate-detection guidance (likely in the planning or decomposition steps).
- `skill/implement/SKILL.md` — Add duplicate-detection guidance (likely before worktree creation or early review).

## Related work

- **AH-0MTVYB4L900286VT** — "Player should be a shape that shows direction" (AI_Hell) — This was the motivating example: a duplicate of **AH-0MTAF76Q1008BLBE** "Direction-neutral ship shape" which was already shipped. The intake skill identified it as a duplicate and auto-completed it, but there was no explicit prior guidance on how to handle this situation.
- **SA-0MS9B8WDT0061G97** — "Add test anti-pattern guidance to implement skill" — Similar pattern: adding procedural guidance to a skill file.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Scope creep:** Adding too much detail could bloat the SKILL.md files and push agents over context windows. Mitigation: keep sections concise and well-scoped.
- **Assumption:** The agent's search capabilities (`wl search`, `wl list`) are sufficient to find duplicate candidates. No new tooling or scripts needed.
- **Assumption:** Agents will follow the guidance. This is a documentation change, not an enforcement mechanism.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 — Scope:** "Should this guidance apply to all skills (intake, plan, implement, and possibly audit/plan) or only the three named skills?" — **Answer (user):** "intake, plan, and implement — those three." Source: user request.
- **Q2 — Delete vs close:** "Should agents delete or close duplicate items?" — **Answer (user):** "close with a reason explaining the duplicate — deletion is permanent, close preserves the history." Source: user request.

data.description:
# Add project title to standup report template

## Problem Statement

The standup skill report header is generic: `## Standup Report (11th September 2026)`.
When standup reports from multiple projects are viewed together, there is no
indication of which project the report belongs to. The opening line should
include the project name: `## <project_name> Standup Report (11th September 2026)`.

## Users

- **Operator reviewing standups across projects** — needs to tell at a glance
  which project a standup report belongs to.

### User Stories

- As an operator, I want the standup report title to start with the project
  name so I can distinguish reports from different projects.
- As an operator, I want the spoken/TTS form to remain natural when the
  project name is included.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The report header rendered by `generate_standup.py` (`format_report`) is
   `## <project_name> Standup Report (<spoken date>)` instead of
   `## Standup Report (<spoken date>)` (e.g. `## SorraAgents Standup Report
   (11th September 2026)`).
2. `<project_name>` is resolved from the target project (e.g. worklog config
   `projectName`, with a sensible fallback such as the project root directory
   name when config is unavailable) and works with `--worklog-dir` /
   `WL_WORKLOG_DIR` from any cwd.
3. The `--json` output includes the resolved project name (or the header
   reflects it) so downstream consumers can use it.
4. `skill/standup/SKILL.md` Report Structure template and Example are updated
   to show the `<project_name>` prefix.
5. Tests cover: header includes project name, fallback when project name is
   unavailable, and JSON output carries the project name.
6. Full test suite passes with no regressions.

## Constraints

- Keep the spoken date format unchanged (e.g. "11th September 2026", never ISO).
- Keep the report first-person and TTS-friendly; project name must read naturally.
- No preamble/postamble changes — template only gains the project-name prefix.

## Existing State

- `skill/standup/scripts/generate_standup.py` — `format_report()` builds
  `## Standup Report ({format_date_tts(now)})`.
- `skill/standup/SKILL.md` — Report Structure and Example show
  `## Standup Report (5th September 2026)` with no project name.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/standup/scripts/generate_standup.py` — resolve project name, update `format_report` header, expose in JSON.
- `skill/standup/SKILL.md` — update Report Structure template and Example.
- `skill/standup/tests/` — new/updated tests for prefixed header.

## Summary

`_parse_key_files_section()` in `skill/plan/plan_helpers.py` collects bullet
lines after a `**Key Files:**` marker but only terminates the section on a
`**`-prefixed line or EOF. It does **not** stop at Markdown ATX headings
(`##`, `###`). As a result, bullet lists in later sections — for example
`## Acceptance Criteria` items that embed backticked code — are parsed as
Key Files entries, producing spurious validation failures such as:

```
Path 'mod.main()' is missing a directory separator ('/')
```

Observed during `/skill:plan SA-0MTYJ5VFI003PZMI`, where the AC bullet
`- [ ] \`mod.main()\` is still invoked ...` produced a false Key Files error
until the section was reordered to the end of the description.

## Impact

Plan/intake review stage 2 (Completeness review) may report false Key Files
defects for otherwise-valid work-item descriptions, forcing authors to
reorder content as a workaround.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `_parse_key_files_section()` terminates at any Markdown ATX heading line (`#` through `######`), not only `**`-prefixed lines.
- [ ] A regression test covers a description with `**Key Files:**` followed by `## Acceptance Criteria` containing backticked bullets, asserting no false-positive paths are extracted.
- [ ] Existing `plan_helpers` Key Files validation tests continue to pass.

Discovered-from: SA-0MTYJ5VFI003PZMI

## Problem

The standup skill (`skill/standup/scripts/generate_standup.py`, default output added in
SA-0MTVB0NAQ007UKID) writes its generated report to `./standups/YYYY_MM_DD.md` in the
project root, but the repository's tracked `.gitignore` does **not** ignore `standups/`.

Consequently any generated standup report appears as an untracked file in the main
checkout, e.g.:

```
$ git status --porcelain=v1 -b
## dev...origin/dev
?? standups/
```

## Impact

`implement.py start` / `implement.py finish` gate on a clean working tree
(`git_has_dirty_files()` treats any non-`.worklog/` entry, including untracked files,
as dirty). An untracked `standups/` directory therefore **blocks the implement workflow
for every agent** until it is removed or excluded, even though it is machine-generated
output and not user-authored work.

Observed: `/skill:implement SA-0MTYJ4MGO007O22W` could not start its first child
(blocked at the dirty-tree gate). The implement skill's dirty-main-checkout guidance
says untracked files that do not prevent worktree creation should be handled by
isolating work in a worktree without touching them; the deterministic script instead
hard-fails. A local, reversible `.git/info/exclude` entry (`standups/`) was added during
that session to unblock.

## Expected

`standups/` is listed in the tracked `.gitignore` so generated standup output never
pollutes `git status` or blocks the implement dirty-tree gate. (If standup reports are
ever intended to be committed, the generator should write somewhere deliberately
tracked instead.)

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `.gitignore` contains an entry for `standups/` (tracked change, committed to `dev`).
- [ ] With a generated `standups/2026_09_11.md` present, `git status --porcelain` reports
      no untracked `standups/` entry.
- [ ] `implement.py start <id>` is not blocked by a generated standup report.
- [ ] The behaviour is covered by a test (e.g. a test asserting the generated default
      output path is git-ignored) or documented as intentionally untestable.

## Notes

- Discovered during the SA-0MTYJ4MGO007O22W implement session.
- The local `.git/info/exclude` workaround is not shared with other clones/agents, so
  the tracked `.gitignore` change is the durable fix.
data.title: Generated standup output (standups/) is not gitignored, blocking the implement dirty-tree gate

`~/.audit_debug/**` and the worklog export (the RCA for
SA-0MU32H6KY0021SJL needed bespoke scripts). There is no single per-run

run, so future RCAs and dashboards do not need log archaeology.

## Problem

The committed git hooks `.githooks/post-checkout` and `.githooks/post-merge` (worklog:post-pull-hook:v1) delegate to the CENTRAL script:

```sh
exec "/home/rgardler/.config/pi/.githooks/worklog-post-pull" "$@"
```

But `~/.config/pi/.githooks/` does not exist on this machine, so EVERY git checkout/merge errors with `exec: /home/rgardler/.config/pi/.githooks/worklog-post-pull: not found` and the post-pull `wl sync` never runs. `scripts/install_pi.sh` only installs the `pre-push` hook into the project `.githooks/` — it does not install the central script, and no other installer creates `~/.config/pi/.githooks/`.

## Evidence

- `cat ~/.config/pi/.githooks/worklog-post-pull` → No such file or directory (2026-09-19).
- The central script itself is committed in-repo at `.githooks/worklog-post-pull` (runs `wl sync`; skippable via WORKLOG_SKIP_POST_PULL=1).
- Reproduced during recovery: `.githooks/post-checkout: 4: exec: ...: not found` after `git checkout`.

## Suggested fix (installer, no code change to hooks)

1. `mkdir -p ~/.config/pi/.githooks`
2. Install a copy/symlink of the repo's `.githooks/worklog-post-pull` there (e.g. `ln -s <repo>/.githooks/worklog-post-pull ~/.config/pi/.githooks/worklog-post-pull`).
3. Extend `scripts/install_pi.sh` to do this idempotently so fresh environments don't regress (this part is a repo change → implement work item).
4. Verify: `git checkout` in any repo with these hooks no longer errors and `wl sync` runs.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `~/.config/pi/.githooks/worklog-post-pull` exists and is executable.
2. A `git checkout`/merge in this repo completes without a hook `not found` error.
3. `scripts/install_pi.sh` idempotently installs the central hook on fresh environments.
