# Browser suite contention: `TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY=2` lets two full suites starve each other

Discovered while auditing TCE `CG-0MTV69NII000LW8I` — `discovered-from:CG-0MTV69NII000LW8I`.

## Problem
`run_tests.py` bounds concurrent test runs with `TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY` (default **2**, introduced by `SA-0MTG5U75A001F1RG`). Two concurrent full suites — e.g. two `implement.py finish` gates in different TCE worktrees, plus an audit's F3 auto-execution — each spin up a 4-worker Chromium browser stage (`maxWorkers: 4` in `vite.config.ts`). On a single host this oversubscribes CPU/GPU, so timing-sensitive browser tests time out and vitest runs get **SIGKILLed (exit 137)** or **hang (exit 124)**.

## Impact
A repo can go many hours without a green full-suite run, blocking audits/releases and producing misleading `test-failure` items.

**TCE evidence (2026-09-20):** last green full-suite cache entry **~29 h old**; consecutive entries `exit 124 / 137 / 1 / 1`; observed **≥2 concurrent full suites** and **30+ vitest/chromium processes**; load average ~8–12 on 16 cores. `tests/main-street/upgrade-drag-drop.browser.test.ts` fails 3 animation-timeout tests under load while passing **6/6 in isolation** (10.2 s).

## Expected Behaviour
- Full-suite runs (or at least browser-heavy suites) are serialized per repo/host to **1**.
- `TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY` becomes context-aware (browser suites ⇒ 1) or the default drops where a Chromium stage is present.
- `implement.py` full-suite gates acquire the guard and log `queued_at` / `wait_seconds` rather than colliding.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Two full project suites in the same repo never execute their browser stages simultaneously (verified by observing serialized runs / semaphore telemetry).
- [ ] `TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY` (or a browser-stage-specific cap) prevents cross-suite browser starvation; the behaviour is documented.
- [ ] `implement.py` full-suite gates acquire the guard and emit a `queued_at`/`wait_seconds` log line.
- [ ] A TCE full-suite re-run during a multi-agent period yields a green full-suite cache entry.

## Related Work
- `SA-0MTG5U75A001F1RG` — Extend test skill to use shared concurrency primitive (the `TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY` default of 2 this refines).
- `CG-0MUA7RRXL007GEHW` (TCE) — the timing-fragile `upgrade-drag-drop.browser.test.ts` surfaced by this contention.
- `CG-0MTV69NII000LW8I` (TCE) — audit blocked on obtaining a green full-suite run.

## Key Files
- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` — `TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY` handling.
- `skill/shared/process_semaphore.py` / `skill/shared/queue.py` — shared bounded-concurrency primitive.
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — the full-suite finish gate.
data.title: Browser suite contention: TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY=2 lets two full suites starve each other (137 kills / 124 hangs)

# Report renderer reports Children: 0 for parents with children

## Summary

The shared report helper `scripts/render_report.py` (skills/report) fetches work-item data with `wl show <id> --json` and reads the children count from that payload. Because `wl show <id> --json` (without `--children`) does not include the children array, the count is always zero and the canonical end-of-session report renders `Children: 👥 0` even when the item has many children. The report skill's own spec states the Children field source is the `children` array length from `wl show <id> --children --json`.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Create a work item with at least one child.
2. Run `python3 $(skill_path report)/scripts/render_report.py <id> --skill-name plan --headline "..."`.
3. Observe `- **Children:** 👥 0` in the Meta-Data block, even though `wl show <id> --children --json` returns the children.

Concrete example: AH-0MU9LPZ0G0015292 has 11 children at stage `plan_complete`, yet the report rendered on 2026-09-20 shows `Children: 👥 0`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `render_report.py` fetches children via `wl show <id> --children --json` (or otherwise reads the top-level `children` array) when populating the Meta-Data Children count.
- The rendered report shows the real child count for a parent with children (at least 11 for the example above).
- Behaviour for leaf items (no children) remains `Children: 👥 0`.
- Existing report tests pass (updated if they encoded the wrong payload shape).

## Notes

- discovered-from:AH-0MU9LPZ0G0015292 (a plan run exposed the issue; the report was pasted verbatim per the skill so the incorrect count was surfaced to the operator rather than silently corrected).
- File: `/home/rgardler/.pi/agent/skills/report/scripts/render_report.py` (line ~383 `cmd = ["wl", "show", work_item_id, "--json"]`; line ~232 `metadata["Children"] = ...`).

data.description:
The end-of-session report helper (`skill/report/scripts/render_report.py`) always renders **Audit: ❔ not run** in the Meta-Data block, even when the work item has a persisted, passing audit.

### Root cause

`wl show <id> --json` returns `auditResult` as a **top-level** key of the response envelope:

```json
{ "success": true, "workItem": { ... }, "auditResult": { "readyToClose": true, ... }, "comments": [...] }
```

`render_metadata()` reads `work_item.get("auditResult")` (line ~235), where `work_item = data.get("workItem", {})` — the top-level `auditResult` is never consulted, so the lookup is always falsy and the audit status degrades to "not run".

Discovered while rendering the final report for SA-0MU7FD0YF0065EG9, whose audit had passed (`readyToClose: true`, all 4 ACs met) yet the report showed "Audit: not run".

### Acceptance Criteria

1. `render_metadata()` resolves audit status from the top-level `auditResult` of the `wl show --json` envelope (falling back to any `workItem.auditResult` for backward compatibility), so a `readyToClose: true` result renders as passed and `readyToClose: false` renders as failed.
2. A unit test covers: top-level `auditResult` with `readyToClose: true` → "passed"; `readyToClose: false` → "failed"; absent/null → "not run".
3. `--json` (stdin) mode continues to work for callers that pass a bare work-item dict.

---

## Problem Statement

Agents repeatedly make the same mistakes when working with pi — using `skill_path` as a bash command instead of the tool, expanding backticks in shell commands, forgetting Python imports, and falling into self-correction loops. A skill that analyses recent session logs to detect these patterns would enable proactive skill improvements and prevent recurring failures.

## Users

- **Agent operator / PI** — receives a structured report of agent confusion patterns and actionable improvement recommendations.
- **Skill authors** — get targeted work items to update SKILL.md files, scripts, or add guardrails.
- **Producers** — understand systemic agent behaviour issues across the project.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Skill reads the last 20 session logs (`.pi/agent/sessions/<project-slug>/*.jsonl`) for the CWD project, sorted by modification time.
2. Heuristic analysis extracts: tool call distribution, thinking-content error signals (keywords: error, fail, retry, incorrect, sorry, wrong, fix, correct, issue, problem, confused, wait, actually, oh, hmm, ah), tool result errors (tracebacks, permission denied, command not found, shell expansion errors), and retry/self-correction patterns.
3. LLM-assisted interpretation (via pi calls) classifies patterns into categories (e.g. "skill invocation confusion", "shell quoting issues", "Python import omissions", "permission issues") and generates recommendations.
4. Structured report rendered in the agent response with: summary of findings, top patterns by frequency, recommended skill improvements, and evidence citations (which sessions showed which patterns).
5. Recommendations are filed as worklog comments on the parent work item.
6. For each actionable recommendation, a child work item is auto-created with issue-type `chore` or `feature`, assigned to Map, and linked via `related-to:<parent-id>` in the description.
7. The skill follows existing project conventions: `skill/agent-log-review/SKILL.md`, `skill/agent-log-review/scripts/`, `skill/agent-log-review/tests/`.
8. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries (e.g. `docs/dev/agent-log-review-skill-reference.md`).
9. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Hybrid approach: heuristics for extraction, LLM for classification — not fully automated LLM-only (too expensive) and not heuristic-only (too noisy).
- Only CWD project sessions; no cross-project analysis.
- Auto-create work items but don't implement them — that's downstream work.
- Must handle v3 session log format (session, model_change, thinking_level_change, message types with content as list of thinking/toolCall parts).

## Existing State

- Session logs exist at `~/.pi/agent/sessions/<project-slug>/*.jsonl` in v3 format.
- Existing skills follow `SKILL.md` + `scripts/` + `tests/` convention.
- Related work: SA-0MSNYWMJJ002CIJ7 (tag pi sessions spawned from skills with `--session-id`), SA-0MSMC8KRS00164VD (24h experiment: measure session length & token use), SA-0MU32H6KY0021SJL (RCA and reliability recommendations for audit failures), SA-0MLGZN2IH0HH6JSH (Add 'waiting_for_input' session state).
- Known patterns already visible in current sessions: backtick expansion in bash commands, `skill_path` used as bash command, Python `NameError`/`KeyError` from missing imports, `python` vs `python3`, permission denied on script execution, self-correction loops in thinking content.

## Desired Change

A reusable skill that agents can invoke (e.g. `/skill:agent-log-review`) to periodically analyse session logs, produce reports, and auto-create improvement work items.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/agent-log-review/SKILL.md` — skill definition and invocation docs
- `skill/agent-log-review/scripts/agent_log_review.py` — main analysis script
- `skill/agent-log-review/tests/test_agent_log_review.py` — unit tests
- `docs/dev/agent-log-review-skill-reference.md` — skill reference docs

## Risks & Assumptions

**Assumptions**
- Pi v3 session log format is stable (fields: `session`, `model_change`, `thinking_level_change`, `message` with list content of `thinking`/`toolCall` parts, `toolResult` role).
- `<project-slug>` session directory is derived deterministically from CWD (e.g. `--home-rgardler-projects-SorraAgents--`).
- 20 sessions is a statistically useful sample size for common patterns.

**Risks & mitigations**
- **LLM cost/latency** — 20 logs total several MB; mitigate by sending only distilled heuristic signals (counts, excerpts) to the LLM, not raw logs.
- **False positives** — keyword heuristics over-trigger on legitimate uses of "error" (e.g. error-handling code). Mitigate with context windows and LLM confirmation before filing work items.
- **Huge individual sessions** — streaming line-by-line parse, cap per-session excerpt size.
- **Privacy** — session logs may contain paths/tokens; redact secrets in the report and never persist raw log content outside `.worklog/tmp/`.
- **Scope creep** — do not build auto-fix/auto-edit of skills; keep to report + work-item creation (extra opportunities become linked, not in-scope).

## Related work

- SA-0MSNYWMJJ002CIJ7 — Skills: tag pi sessions spawned from skills with --session-id (helps identify skill-spawned sessions for analysis)
- SA-0MSMC8KRS00164VD — 24h experiment: AGENTS.md STE100 instruction — measure session length & token use vs previous period (analysis pattern)
- SA-0MU32H6KY0021SJL — RCA and reliability recommendations: why audit Phase 1/Phase 2 frequently fail (similar RCA approach)
- SA-0MLGZN2IH0HH6JSH — Add 'waiting_for_input' session state (session analysis infrastructure)

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Analysis engine — what approach for pattern detection (heuristic only / LLM-assisted / hybrid)?" — Answer (operator): "hybrid". Source: interactive reply. Research: confirmed existing skills use pi calls (e.g. audit Phase 2) so LLM calls from a skill are an established pattern.
- Q: "Scope — which projects' logs, and where should the report go?" — Answer (operator): "the project from which the skill is initiated (CWD), recommendations filed in the worklog, report returned in agent response". Source: interactive reply.
- Q: "Recommendations — should the skill auto-create work items, or report-only?" — Answer (operator): "create". Source: interactive reply.
- Q: "Permission to create the work item?" — Answer (operator): implied by invoking `/intake` with the seed intent; item SA-0MUEKTJRD0010CGC created. Source: interactive invocation.

# tree_coverage truncates wrapped AC bullets

## Discovery

Found while planning SA-0MUG0WFP8008WN63: the AC-coverage review reported `coverage_pct: 0.0`
and `recommendation: stop` even though every parent AC is genuinely covered by a child. Root
cause: `extract_acceptance_criteria()` in `skill/shared/tree_coverage.py` captures only the first
physical line of each `- ` bullet. Work-item descriptions wrap their AC bullets (as the global
`AGENTS.md`/intake/plan conventions produce), so the parent ACs handed to the Jaccard matcher are
truncated mid-sentence:

```
'**AC1 — Hermetic git usage:** every test helper that runs real `git` commands'
```

instead of the full criterion. The child ACs are truncated the same way, and the resulting
similarity scores (0.14-0.28) fall below the 0.4 threshold, producing a false `stop` that blocks
`plan_complete`. This is also consistent with the earlier observation recorded on
SA-0MUG0WFP8008WN63 that keeping an auxiliary item as a `wl` child made coverage report `stop`.

## Goal

Wrapped acceptance-criteria bullets are extracted whole, so the coverage review measures real
coverage rather than first-line snippets.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1** `extract_acceptance_criteria()` joins continuation lines of a wrapped `- ` bullet until
  the next blank line, next bullet, or next `##` heading, and returns the full criterion text.
  *Verification:* a unit test with a multi-line wrapped AC asserts the full text is returned.
- **AC2** A regression test reproduces the observed failure: a parent with wrapped ACs and a child
  whose mapping bullet restates the *full* parent AC yields `fully_covered: True`; and the
  pre-fix behaviour (first-line-only) is covered by an explicit test asserting the fix (not by
  asserting the bug).
- **AC3** Backwards compatibility: descriptions whose ACs are already single-line return identical
  results (`skill/shared/tests/test_tree_coverage.py` stays green, extended as needed).
- **AC4** The similarity threshold semantics are documented in the module docstring: tokens are
  lowercased/punctuation-stripped, and parent/child AC text is compared as whole criteria.

## Key Files

- `skill/shared/tree_coverage.py` — `extract_acceptance_criteria`, `compute_coverage`, `resolve_coverage_gaps`.
- `skill/shared/tests/test_tree_coverage.py` — regression tests.
- `docs/dev/plan-skill-reference.md` — note the mapping convention (child ACs should restate the
  parent criterion they cover).

## Notes

- Discovered during planning of SA-0MUG0WFP8008WN63. Workaround applied in that plan: each child
  carries an explicit `Covers parent ACn — ...` bullet restating the parent AC's first line, which
  lifts the Jaccard score to ~0.8 and lets the review return `proceed` (100%).
- A real fix should not require the workaround wording.

- **discovered-from:** SA-0MUG0WFP8008WN63
data.title: tree_coverage truncates wrapped AC bullets

## Problem statement

Discovered during the find-related v3 review (discovered-from:SA-0MNCDAQ8W008KOG9).

The v3 overhaul reduced search subprocesses from 523 to 8 and wall-clock from a 240s+ timeout to ~3s on the *measurement machine*. Re-measured on a typical development machine, wall-clock is **~5-6s**, which exceeds the skill's documented <5s expectation.

## Evidence

- Measured runs (work item SA-0MNCDAQ8W008KOG9): 5.28s, 5.62s (warm); 9.85s (first cold run).
- Phase breakdown: `wl show` ~0.32s; semantic probe ~0.45s; **8 sequential `wl search` calls ~3.43s** (~0.43s each); repo scan (421 files) ~0.34s; `wl update` ~0.39s.
- The dominant cost is per-subprocess latency of the 8 sequential searches (96% of v2 runtime was also subprocess waits).

## Proposed improvement

- Parallelise the 8 per-keyword `wl search` calls (e.g. a bounded `ThreadPoolExecutor`) — searches are independent, so wall-clock should approach the slowest single call (~0.5s) instead of the sum (~3.4s).
- Alternatively/additionally reduce `MAX_SEARCH_KEYWORDS` (currently 8) if recall permits.
- Re-measure and update the SKILL.md runtime expectations to the measured figure.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] find-related runtime measured at <5s on a representative work item (documented command + output)
- [ ] Recall preserved (no regression in related-item recall for the review work item)
- [ ] SKILL.md runtime expectations match the measured figure
- [ ] Unit/integration tests cover the parallel-search path

## Constraints

- Do not regress idempotency or report compactness (v3 guarantees).
- Keep the per-keyword query strategy (batched queries were measured to collapse conjunctively).
data.title: find-related: bring runtime back under the 5s target

## Problem statement

Discovered during the find-related v3 review (discovered-from:SA-0MNCDAQ8W008KOG9).

Keyword extraction is frequency-ranked and capped to the top 8 (`MAX_SEARCH_KEYWORDS`), but the highest-frequency terms are generic words, so the search returns weakly related items.

## Evidence

For SA-0MNCDAQ8W008KOG9 ("Review find related skill"), the top-8 search keywords were:

`skill, related, work, find, report, improvements, item, keyword`

Related work items returned: 2 of 3 were unrelated low-severity lint items about `find_related.py` (C401) and 1 was an unrelated intake/plan refactor. Repo file matches were audit documentation files (`skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`, `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md`, `skill/audit/SKILL.md`) matched on generic words such as "acceptance", "criteria", "report".

The full extracted keyword list is 155 terms; only the top 8 are used. Generic corpus-wide terms dominate the ranking because raw frequency is used without an inverse-document-frequency (IDF) adjustment.

## Proposed improvement

- Weight keywords by inverse document frequency (or equivalent) so distinctive domain terms outrank corpus-generic words.
- Boost title terms over body/description terms.
- Expand the stop-word list with project-generic terms ("work", "item", "report", "review", "skill") where they add no signal.
- Optionally require a minimum relevance threshold before listing a related item.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] For SA-0MNCDAQ8W008KOG9, at least 2 of the top-3 related items are genuinely related to the find-related skill (manual reviewer judgement, documented)
- [ ] Keyword selection is deterministic across re-runs (idempotency preserved)
- [ ] Existing find-related unit tests pass; new tests assert the ranking behaviour
- [ ] No increase in runtime beyond the v3 bound (subprocess count remains capped)

## Constraints

- Preserve the v3 feedback-loop fix (report section stripped before extraction; no unbounded keyword growth).
- Conservative policy: prefer false negatives over false positives.
data.title: find-related: improve keyword relevance (IDF/title weighting)

## Problem
The main checkout has a stale LOCAL branch literally named `origin/dev` (`refs/heads/origin/dev`), separate from the remote-tracking ref `refs/remotes/origin/dev`. Git treats the unqualified name `origin/dev` as ambiguous (warning) and resolves it to the local branch.

Impact:
- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` `_resolve_merge_base()` uses the unqualified `origin/dev` base ref, so changed-file detection diffs against the stale local branch and reports the entire repository as changed — breaking changed-scope test selection.
- `implement.py` changed-scope fallback then runs the full suite (observed during SA-0MUGX1DIT000M7S1).
- Any command using unqualified `origin/<branch>` can silently target the wrong ref.

## Evidence
During SA-0MUGX1DIT000M7S1: `git diff --name-only origin/dev` listed the entire repo; `git for-each-ref` showed both `refs/heads/origin/dev` (ea13571) and `refs/remotes/origin/dev`.

## Expected / options
- Clean up accidental local branches that shadow remote-tracking refs (operator decision — do not delete without permission).
- Harden ref resolution to prefer fully-qualified `refs/remotes/origin/<branch>` (the SA-0MUGX1DIT000M7S1 sync helper already does this) and/or detect the ambiguous-ref warning.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Unqualified `origin/<branch>` resolution in changed-scope/test tooling is unambiguous (fully-qualified remote-tracking ref preferred).
- [ ] A regression test covers a local branch shadowing `origin/<branch>`.
- [ ] The stale branch is triaged (restored/deleted) with operator approval.

Discovered during SA-0MUGX1DIT000M7S1.
data.title: Stale local branch named origin/dev makes origin/dev ambiguous and breaks changed-scope test selection

# Problem statement

The audit runner's parent-first flow re-audits all children on every run because the freshness fingerprint includes the global git HEAD sha. In `--child-in-main-slot` mode, non-interactive runs leave all children with `partial` verdicts, which blocks the parent from recording a "Ready to close: Yes" result even when all parent ACs are met. This prevents audit completion for epics whose children were previously audited.

# Users

- **Audit runner / downtime worker** — expects a non-interactive audit of an epic to produce a valid verdict without requiring a live agent session.
- **Producer / human reviewer** — expects the audit to accurately reflect whether work is ready to close, not to block on stale or unserviced child verdicts.

# Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Fingerprint scoping.** `_compute_content_fingerprint` no longer includes the global git HEAD sha as a sole invalidation trigger; instead it is scoped to child-relevant key files and/or commits so that unrelated HEAD movement on `dev` does not invalidate previously valid child audits.
- **AC2 — In-main-slot partial verdict handling.** When a child's `ac_results` remain `partial` because the invoking agent session never serviced the `[AUDIT_IN_MAIN_SLOT_WORK]` items, the parent audit treats those verdicts as "not assessed" (inherits the child's previously stored verdict or marks them reusable) rather than blocking the parent's readiness-to-close decision.
- **AC3 — Diagnostic clarity.** The audit output surfaces a clear, machine-parseable diagnostic that distinguishes a "child partial because unserviced in-main-slot" verdict from a genuine "not-ready" child verdict, including the reason code in the audit summary.
- **AC4 — No regression on interactive runs.** The above fixes do not change the behaviour of interactive audit runs (where an agent session *can* service in-main-slot items); those continue to honour the full in-main-slot workflow.
- **AC5 — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.** Run the complete suite and confirm zero failures.

# Constraints

- The fix must not introduce a new mode flag or require operator configuration; it should be the default behaviour.
- The fix should be backward-compatible with persisted audit results (old fingerprint format should still be readable).
- The change scope is the audit runner's child freshness logic (`_compute_content_fingerprint`, `_child_content_changed`), the in-main-slot verdict accumulation logic (`_build_issue_json`, `all_ac_acceptable`), and the diagnostic output path.

# Existing state

- `_compute_content_fingerprint` includes the current git HEAD sha — any new commit on `dev` invalidates every stored child audit.
- In `child_in_main_slot=True` mode, child Phase-1 AC screens and Phase-2 deep analysis emit `[AUDIT_IN_MAIN_SLOT_WORK]` items for the invoking session. In non-interactive runs, these are never serviced and stay `partial`.
- `_build_issue_json` includes child AC verdicts in `all_ac_acceptable`, so the parent is reported "Ready to close: No" even when all parent ACs are met.
- The runner's terminal lifecycle then demotes parent and children to `open`/`plan_complete` as a side effect.

# Desired change

1. **Scope the fingerprint**: Replace the global HEAD sha in `_compute_content_fingerprint` with a child-scoped hash (key files + relevant commits).
2. **Handle partial verdicts**: When computing `all_ac_acceptable`, skip children whose verdict is `partial` due to unserviced in-main-slot items — treat them as "not assessed" rather than "not accepted."
3. **Add diagnostics**: In the audit summary, emit a reason code or flag indicating when a child's `partial` verdict is due to unserviced in-main-slot items vs. genuine assessment failure.

# Key Files (predicted)

- `src/audit/` or equivalent audit runner module — `_compute_content_fingerprint`, `_child_content_changed`, `_build_issue_json`, in-main-slot verdict handling
- `scripts/audit_runner*` or equivalent — runner invocation, non-interactive path
- Audit output/summary formatter — diagnostic message generation

# Related work

- **AH-0MUD8E015004C4JO** — Unify PlayScene/GymFormationScene combat logic (completed): the parent epic that discovered this issue during audit.
- **SA-0MSKB6VJA005N43F** — Audit parent-first flow (internal assertion): the flow that triggers the re-audit on stale children.
- **SA-0MT2XRGEU0009QRE** — Audit in-main-slot mode (internal assertion): the mode that creates `[AUDIT_IN_MAIN_SLOT_WORK]` items.

# Risks & assumptions

- **Risk — fingerprint scoping is incomplete.** If child-relevant files/commits are not correctly identified, stale audits may still be invalidated or, conversely, genuinely stale audits may be reused. Mitigation: carefully identify the key files that each child audit covers; add a test case that simulates unrelated HEAD movement vs. child-relevant HEAD movement.
- **Risk — inheriting stale child verdicts masks real regressions.** If a child's code changed but the fingerprint didn't catch it, inheriting an old verdict is incorrect. Mitigation: the fingerprint scoping should cover all files relevant to the child audit.
- **Assumption:** all three suggested directions are desired (fingerprint scoping, partial-verdict handling, diagnostic clarity).
- **Assumption:** the audit runner is a Node.js/TypeScript or Python tool within the project; the fix applies to the runner's Python/TS source.
data.title: Audit: parent-first flow re-audits stale children and blocks on unserviced in-main-slot verdicts

## Summary

While running `pytest skill/audit/tests/` from an agent worktree, the repo-root live-repo mutation guard (`skill/shared/live_repo_guard.py`, F5 SA-0MUG30JSE0069JEQ) failed session teardown with:

```
live-repo mutation detected during skill/audit/tests/test_budget_baseline.py::TestDeriveBudgetBaseline::test_multiple_phases:
  deleted ref    refs/stash (54e6a9b1725a781f5a092f572c8d46529e10c546)
```

The named test is a pure-function test with no git calls, so the attribution is a false positive: `refs/stash` is a **shared** ref across all git worktrees, so any concurrent agent/worktree running a stash operation (or a stash-touching test) mutates the ref the guard snapshots. The stash commit object survived and was restored with `git stash store`, so no data was lost.

## Impact

- Spurious test-suite failures (non-deterministic) for any test session run while another worktree mutates `refs/stash`.
- Potential data-loss risk if a concurrent `git stash drop`/clear removes a shared stash while another agent is mid-run.
- The guard's `offender` attribution names an unrelated test, making triage confusing.

## Acceptance criteria

1. `refs/stash` mutations that cannot be attributed to the running test session are either excluded from the guard fingerprint or reported as a non-fatal warning (never fail the session for another worktree's stash churn).
2. Concurrent mutations of shared refs (stash, notes, remotes) from another worktree do not fail an unrelated test session.
3. A regression test covers two concurrent worktrees where one mutates `refs/stash` while the other runs the guard.

## Notes

- Discovered-from: SA-0MTJ0KO6L004GIZK (observed during its implementation test run).
- Repo: SorraAgents. Guard root is the worktree root; `git worktree list --porcelain` already excludes `.worklog/worktrees/` branches — but the shared stash ref is not branch-scoped.
data.title: Live-repo guard: shared refs/stash causes spurious mutation failures across concurrent worktrees

## Summary

`skill/plan/plan_helpers.py::plan-approval-gate` fails to request producer approval for items whose effort is a t-shirt size (XS/S/M/L/XL) or whose risk is `Severe`. The skill contract states "Absent effort/risk → default conservatively to requesting approval (a human checkpoint is never silently skipped)" and the gate should request approval when effort is Medium/Large/Extra Large OR risk is High or higher — but the vocabulary sets do not match the values `wl` actually stores.

Discovered during planning of **SA-0MUIA3OE40001QJX** (effort `M`, risk `Severe`): the gate returned `request_approval: false`, so a Severe-risk security/data-loss item would have silently skipped the human checkpoint. The plan session escalated manually instead.

**discovered-from:SA-0MUIA3OE40001QJX**

## Evidence

- `wl show SA-0MUIA3OE40001QJX --json` → `"effort": "M"`, `"risk": "Severe"`.
- `python3 skill/plan/plan_helpers.py plan-approval-gate SA-0MUIA3OE40001QJX` → `{"request_approval": false, ...}` before this work item was raised.
- `PLAN_APPROVAL_EFFORT` contains full words (`Medium`, `Large`, `Extra Large`); `PLAN_APPROVAL_RISK` contains only `High`.

## Proposed fix

- Normalise effort (accept both `M`/`Medium` etc.) and include `Severe` in the risk set, or compare against the canonical `wl` value vocabulary.
- Add unit tests covering every effort/risk combination, including the absent-value conservative default.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `plan-approval-gate` returns `request_approval: true` for effort `M`/`L`/`XL` and for risk `High`/`Severe`, using the values `wl` stores.
- [ ] Both t-shirt abbreviations and full words are accepted for effort.
- [ ] Absent/unrecognised effort or risk still defaults conservatively to requesting approval.
- [ ] Unit tests cover the full effort × risk matrix, including the `M`/`Severe` case from SA-0MUIA3OE40001QJX.

**Key Files:**
- skill/plan/plan_helpers.py
- skill/plan/tests/test_plan_helpers.py

# audit_runner failure-restore reuses an invalid pre-audit status/stage combo, leaving items unrecoverable

## Problem statement

When an audit ends in an infrastructure-failure / fallback-tainted "Ready to close: No" verdict, `audit_runner.py` restores the captured pre-audit `status`+`stage` verbatim. If that captured combination is already invalid (which happens when an item was imported/refiled with status and stage set independently), every restore attempt is rejected by `wl` and the item is left in an unresolved, inconsistent state.

Observed during the audit of SA-0MUFM54CA0010LVD on 2026-09-26 (session herdr-1790437388-2668941-15858, log `/home/rgardler/.audit_debug/SorraAgents/SA-0MUFM54CA0010LVD-20260926-173301.log`):

- Phase 1 parent screening hit audit-concurrency starvation → unparseable → infra-fallback `partial` for all ACs.
- `_apply_terminal_lifecycle` correctly chose the restore branch, building `wl update <id> --status blocked --stage in_review`.
- The captured combo was invalid (`blocked` is not compatible with `in_review`), so all 3 attempts failed.
- The runner printed "the item's lifecycle is unresolved" and exited non-zero.

The item's pre-audit status was already invalid (`in-progress`/`in_review`; `wl` allows stage `in_review` only with status `completed`).

## Root cause

`_apply_terminal_lifecycle` (~L10960) and `_restore_pre_audit_state_on_failure` (~L10828) only substitute a safe stage when `safe_stage` is falsy (i.e. `ctx.original_stage` was never captured). A present-but-invalid captured combo is used as-is, so the restore cannot succeed and the item is stranded.

## Desired change

Before applying a restore (or a "No" demotion), validate the intended `(status, stage)` pair against `wl`'s allowed combinations and coerce to the nearest valid pair (e.g. keep the status but fall back to `plan_complete`/`intake_complete`/`idea` for non-completed statuses), or retry with a stage-agnostic update. Never leave an item in an invalid combination after the runner exits.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. When the captured pre-audit `(status, stage)` combination is invalid, the failure/restore path applies a valid, consistent state instead of failing all attempts, and the runner never leaves the item in an invalid combination.
2. A regression test covers restoring an item whose captured combo is invalid (e.g. `blocked`/`in_review`) and asserts a valid terminal state is reached.
3. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
4. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- The fix must not alter the semantic intent of the restore: preserve the captured status (e.g. `blocked` stays `blocked`) and only coerce the stage when the combination is invalid.
- The valid status/stage mapping is defined in `config.js` (`statusStageCompatibility`):
  - `open` → `idea`, `intake_complete`, `plan_complete`
  - `in-progress` → `intake_complete`, `plan_complete`
  - `input_needed` → `idea`, `intake_complete`, `plan_complete`
  - `blocked` → `idea`, `intake_complete`, `plan_complete`
  - `completed` → `in_review`, `done`
  - `deleted` → `idea`, `intake_complete`, `plan_complete`, `done`
- The fix should be self-contained in the audit runner's restore logic; no changes to `wl` itself.

## Existing state

Two locations apply the restore:
1. `_restore_pre_audit_state_on_failure` (~L10828) — standalone restore after verification failure.
2. `_apply_terminal_lifecycle` (~L10960) — primary restore path in the verdict-driven transition.

Both follow the same pattern:
```python
safe_status = ctx.original_status or "open"
safe_stage = ctx.original_stage
if not safe_stage:
    safe_stage = "in_review" if safe_status == "completed" else "plan_complete"
```

This only handles the case where `original_stage` was never captured. When `original_stage` exists but is incompatible with `original_status`, the combo is invalid and rejected by `wl`.

## Desired change (implementation)

Introduce a helper function `_coerce_valid_status_stage(status, stage)` that:
1. Validates the `(status, stage)` pair against the `statusStageCompatibility` map.
2. Returns `(status, stage)` unchanged if valid.
3. If invalid, keeps the captured status but falls back to a valid stage:
   - For non-`completed` statuses: `plan_complete` (the closest "work in progress" stage).
   - For `completed`: `in_review`.
4. Logs a warning when coercion occurs, so operators know the original state was non-standard.

Apply this helper in both `_restore_pre_audit_state_on_failure` and `_apply_terminal_lifecycle` before building the `wl update` command.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Coercion changes the restored state slightly.** The stage may shift (e.g. `in_review` → `plan_complete` for a `blocked` item). This is intentional and safer than leaving the item unrecoverable. Operators should note the warning message.
- **The `statusStageCompatibility` mapping lives in ContextHub's `config.js`, not SorraAgents.** The audit runner must not import from ContextHub. Valid combos should be inlined in `audit_runner.py` (or sourced from a shared constant in `skill/shared/`). This is a deliberate isolation choice.
- **Scope creep risk:** Only fix the restore path — do not address all status/stage issues in the runner (e.g. the "No" demotion path or the "Yes" advance path, which already produce valid combos). Source: explicit scope from the original report.

## Related work

- **SA-0MSG9SLGI002OF7V** — "Audit runner demotes in_review item to open/plan_complete on infrastructure-failure fallback verdicts" — the prior fix that added the `fallback_tainted` flag and restore path. This issue is a follow-up: the restore itself fails when the captured combo is invalid.
- **SA-0MUFM54CA0010LVD** — the item that exposed the bug during audit.
- **SA-0MS99053T001ED0C** — "find-related and refactor skills still flip status to completed via StatusLifecycle" — related StatusLifecycle correctness issue.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1:** When coercing an invalid `(status, stage)` pair, should we preserve the captured status or also attempt to adjust the status? — **Answer (Map):** Preserve the captured status and only coerce the stage. The status carries the item's operational state (blocked/in-progress/open) which should not be silently altered. Source: analysis of the `statusStageCompatibility` mapping.
- **Q2:** Should the coercion helper be placed in `audit_runner.py` or shared (`status_lifecycle.py`)? — **Answer (Map):** Place it in `audit_runner.py` for now; if `status_lifecycle.py` needs the same logic (e.g. for general wl validation), refactor to shared later. Source: current usage is audit-runner-specific.
- **Q3:** What log level should coercion warnings use? — **Answer (Map):** `print(..., file=sys.stderr)` (consistent with existing error paths in the runner). Source: audit_runner.py convention.

`skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_merge_gate.py` through the shared sandbox

`conftest.py`) detects and fails a run if the live checkout is mutated, so this
is defence-in-depth rather than an unguarded hole — but the helpers themselves
are still non-hermetic.

subprocess.run(["git", "config", "user.email", "test@test.com"], cwd=..., check=True, ...)
subprocess.run(["git", "config", "user.name", "Test"], cwd=..., check=True, ...)

# Remove residual fixture identity from the live checkout `.git/config`

**discovered-from:** SA-0MUG0WFP8008WN63 (SorraAgents)

## Context

The 2026-09-24 live-repo corruption incident (SA-0MUG0WFP8008WN63) left fixture
artefacts in the main checkout. The companion cleanup (SA-0MUG216UP008821M)
removed the fixture branches/refs and `root-file-repo/`, but the audit
(2026-09-26, ready-to-close: No run) found a **residual fixture identity** still
present in the live checkout's local git config:

    user.name  = T
    user.email = t@t.com

This was not enumerated by parent AC4's branch/ref/`root-file-repo/` checks, so
it was recorded as a non-blocking caveat. It causes commits made in the live
checkout to be attributed to the fixture identity rather than the operator's
global identity.

## Desired change

Remove the residual repo-local identity overrides so the live checkout falls
back to the operator's global git identity:

    git config --local --unset user.name
    git config --local --unset user.email

Verify with `git config --local --get user.name` (empty) and
`git config --global --get user.name` (operator identity).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The live SorraAgents checkout has no repo-local `user.name` / `user.email`
      overrides; `git config --local --list` shows neither key.
- [ ] The operator's global identity is effective in the live checkout
      (`git config user.name` returns the global value).
- [ ] No other fixture config keys remain in the live checkout's local config
      (`core.hooksPath`, `core.bare` re-checked).

## Notes

This is a live-environment cleanup (not a code change); it must be performed on
the main checkout with operator awareness.

data.description:
## Summary

The 2026-09-26 leaked-`GIT_DIR` incident (SA-0MUIA3OE40001QJX) was rooted in a repository-override git environment variable exported into agent/test sessions by a launcher **outside** the `skill/` tree. Defence-in-depth now neutralises the *effect* at every in-repo execution path, but the launcher can still export a live-repo `GIT_DIR` (plus `GIT_WORK_TREE` / `GIT_CONFIG*`) into the **pre-scrub** environment of any process that calls `git` directly. This item investigates that export and removes or scopes it at its source.

## Problem statement

On 2026-09-26 an orphaned audit fan-out inherited `GIT_DIR=<live worktree git dir>`, `GIT_EXEC_PATH=/usr/lib/git-core` and `GIT_PREFIX=` from a launcher outside the `skill/` tree. The in-repo defence-in-depth layers (shared env scrub, release-gate fail-fast, host-wide audit cap) stop that value from reaching test subprocesses, but they remain the only protection: anything spawned before the scrub that calls `git` itself can still be redirected into the live checkout. The exporting process has not been identified and no setter exists inside this repository.

## Users

- **Agent operators / maintainers** running autonomous agents through herdr/Pi: need every freshly launched agent/test session to inherit no repository-override git variables.
- **Contributors** sharing the live checkout: need `dev`/`origin/dev` protected even when a launcher is misconfigured.

User stories:

- As an operator, I want a freshly launched agent/test session to inherit no repository-override git variables, so a misconfigured launcher can never redirect a git command into the live checkout.
- As a maintainer, I want the process that sets the override identified and fixed at source, so the defence-in-depth scrub is not the only line of protection.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The exporting process/script is identified with reproducible, non-destructive evidence (environment of a freshly spawned agent session or a traced process ancestry), and the evidence is recorded in the work item.
- [ ] The export is removed or scoped at source so child processes — panes, `audit_runner`, `run_tests`, and direct `git` calls — never inherit a live-repo `GIT_DIR` / `GIT_WORK_TREE` / `GIT_CONFIG*`.
- [ ] A regression check asserts a freshly launched agent/test session has no repository-override variables before any git-touching step; it fails if such a variable is reintroduced.
- [ ] `docs/dev/test-isolation.md` §9.3 (residual launcher risk) is updated to name the confirmed source and the fix, or to record why the source could not be confirmed.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Non-destructive investigation.** The live checkout must never be mutated; evidence gathering must use throwaway/fixture repositories and must never point `GIT_DIR` at the live repo.
- **Source, not symptom.** The fix must be at the exporting launcher, not merely another in-repo scrub layer.
- **Cross-repo.** The likely launcher lives in the ContextHub repository (`packages/herdr`), outside this worklog's repo — see Open Question 1.

## Existing state

Defence-in-depth landed under SA-0MUIA3OE40001QJX:

- `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py` — `REPOSITORY_OVERRIDE_ENV_VARS` + `scrub_repository_overrides` / `repository_override_vars_present` / `log_repository_override_scrub`.
- `skill/test_cache.py::_default_runner`, `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py::_run_cmd`, `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py::_call_pi` pass scrubbed `env=`.
- `run_tests.py --strict-git-env` release-gate fail-fast (invoked by `.githooks/pre-push` for `dev`/`main`).
- `audit_runner.main` host-wide audit cap + `_find_orphaned_audit_processes` / `_warn_on_orphaned_audits`.
- `docs/dev/test-isolation.md` §9.3 documents the residual external-launcher risk.

Confirmed by search (`rg 'export GIT_|GIT_DIR='` across the repo and tooling): **no setter exists in the SorraAgents repository**. Candidate launchers identified:

- **herdr agent launcher** (ContextHub, external): `packages/herdr/shared/send-to-pi.sh` → `packages/herdr/shared/run-pi-agent.sh`, invoked as `herdr pane run <pane> exec bash run-pi-agent.sh <lease> ...`.
- **herdr downtime worker** (external): `buildDowntimeSpawnOptions` in `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` forwards `...process.env` to `send-to-pi.sh`, adding only `HERDR_RESOLVED_CWD` and `AUDIT_PHASE2_PARALLELISM`. It does **not** scrub repository-override vars, so a `GIT_DIR` already present in the herdr process propagates to every spawned pane.
- **git-hook chain** (in repo): `.git/hooks/post-checkout|post-merge|post-rewrite` delegate to `~/.config/pi/.githooks/worklog-post-pull` → `wl sync`. Git sets `GIT_DIR`, `GIT_EXEC_PATH` and `GIT_PREFIX` when running hooks, and `implement.py`'s `git_worktree_add` (`git worktree add`) triggers `post-checkout`. The observed `GIT_EXEC_PATH=/usr/lib/git-core` + empty `GIT_PREFIX` are the exact git-hook signature, so the poisoned environment was most plausibly inherited from a git-spawned child rather than a static shell `export`.

## Desired change

1. Determine the **origin** of `GIT_DIR` in the launcher environment — which process first set it and why — using non-destructive evidence: `/proc/<pid>/environ` of pane/agent/audit processes, git `trace2` (`GIT_TRACE2_EVENT`) around `git worktree add`/hooks, and launcher/hook inspection.
2. Fix at source: scrub (or refuse to propagate) `REPOSITORY_OVERRIDE_ENV_VARS` in the launcher spawn path (e.g. herdr `buildDowntimeSpawnOptions`, `run-pi-agent.sh`/`send-to-pi.sh`) and/or stop the git-hook child that leaks the variables.
3. Add a regression check that a fresh agent/test session has no repository-override variables.
4. Update §9.3 with the finding and fix.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `docs/dev/test-isolation.md` — update §9.3 with the confirmed source and fix.
- `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py` — shared override-var list/scrub helper (reuse for any in-repo mitigation or regression check).
- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` — fresh-session regression check and `--strict-git-env` integration.
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — orphan/env-evidence hooks for reproducing the audit fan-out condition safely.
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `git_worktree_add` flow that triggers the `post-checkout` hook.
- `.githooks/post-checkout`, `.githooks/post-merge`, `.githooks/post-rewrite`, `.githooks/worklog-post-pull` — hook chain (`wl sync`) executed by git with `GIT_DIR`/`GIT_EXEC_PATH`/`GIT_PREFIX` set.
- External (ContextHub, cross-repo — see Open Question 1): `packages/herdr/shared/send-to-pi.sh`, `packages/herdr/shared/run-pi-agent.sh`, `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` (`buildDowntimeSpawnOptions`).

## Related work

- **SA-0MUIA3OE40001QJX** – Test/audit runner leaks GIT_DIR into test subprocesses, corrupting the live checkout and origin/dev (parent incident; completed/in_review).
- Children of SA-0MUIA3OE40001QJX: SA-0MUIULHQC005MUM0 (shared scrub helper), SA-0MUIUMK9Y008SCE0 (scrub in execution paths), SA-0MUIULX49001BWGG (release-gate fail-fast), SA-0MUIULC2Y009XYM1 (regression tests), SA-0MUIUMBL8002HBYH (docs + full suite), SA-0MUIUMO7T00639FL (host-wide audit cap + orphan detection).
- **SA-0MUJ2VMF7000UHCX** – Restore wl sync: main-checkout git identity was left as incident-era `T <t@t.com>` (residual incident recovery).
- **SA-0MUIBWORE001HOLK** – Symlink nested node_modules into implement worktrees (the worktree whose git dir appeared in the leaked `GIT_DIR`).

### Related work (automated report)

- **SA-0MS0DK6BD001RNDG** – implement.py abort script deletes entire project directory when aborting from main working tree (completed)
- **SA-0MSAXHMZT009EHVV** – cwd-independent wl invocation and real diagnostics (completed)
- **SA-0MPDZDVG00013CQJ** – Implement: Agent push-to-dev behavior (completed)

Repository file matches: `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`, `docs/dev/test-isolation.md`, `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md`.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk:** the incident evidence (process env at the time) is gone; reproduction could itself endanger the live checkout. **Mitigation:** use a throwaway repo + `GIT_TRACE2_EVENT`; never point `GIT_DIR` at the live repo.
- **Risk:** fixing only the identified launcher leaves other propagation paths. **Mitigation:** scrub at the launcher spawn boundary (one choke point) plus the regression check.
- **Risk (scope creep):** hardening every launcher is broader than this investigation. **Mitigation:** record additional opportunities as linked work items rather than expanding this item.
- **Assumption:** the leak is architectural (environment propagation through the launcher) rather than a one-off manual `export`.
- **Assumption:** the `GIT_EXEC_PATH`/`GIT_PREFIX` signature indicates a git-spawned child origin; if tracing shows otherwise, the evidence will redirect the fix.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 (scope / repo):** The candidate launchers are external to SorraAgents (ContextHub `packages/herdr`) and the git-hook chain that runs `wl sync`. Where should the fix land? Options: (A) investigate + evidence in SorraAgents (this item); if herdr is the culprit, file a cross-repo ContextHub work item and link it; (B) fix entirely within SorraAgents by hardening the git hooks / adding a wrapper; (C) transfer this item to ContextHub. **Recommended:** A — keeps the incident record in SorraAgents while routing the actual code change to the repo that owns the launcher. — **OPEN QUESTION** (producer input required).
- **Q2 (reproduction):** How much live reproduction is acceptable? Options: (A) non-destructive evidence only (`/proc/<pid>/environ`, launcher/hook inspection, git trace2); (B) also spawn a live agent session and dump its env; (C) both. **Recommended:** C — trace2 + launcher inspection first, then one controlled fresh-session env dump to prove the end-to-end state. — **OPEN QUESTION** (producer input required).
- **Q3 (regression-check placement):** The AC "a freshly launched agent/test session has no repository-override variables" — where should the check live? Options: (A) an in-repo SorraAgents test of the launch wrapper/`run_tests.py`, with the external launcher covered by its own ContextHub test; (B) in-repo only; (C) ContextHub only. **Recommended:** A — each repo tests the boundary it owns. — **OPEN QUESTION** (producer input required).
data.title: Investigate external launcher that exported GIT_DIR into agent/test sessions

# Audit runner: re-auditing an in_review child demotes it and can cascade a parent block

**Discovered-from:** SA-0MUG0WFP8008WN63 (SorraAgents)
**Issue type:** bug · **Priority:** high

## Problem statement

A parent audit can silently demote children that were already `completed` /
`in_review` (and therefore exempt from the parent's child-stage and
child-verdict blocking checks) and then fail its own closure against those
demoted stages — reporting `Ready to close: No` even when every parent
acceptance criterion is `met`. On 2026-09-27, auditing
`SA-0MUG0WFP8008WN63` re-screened three children whose content had changed
because the parent's commit touched files they own; each received a persisted
`Ready to close: No` child audit and was demoted (F2 →
`open`/`plan_complete`, F3 → `blocked`/`plan_complete`, F6 →
`blocked`/`plan_complete`). The parent's own verdict became `No` purely
because those children were no longer exempt, despite all six parent ACs
being `met`.

## Users and user stories

- **Audit operator** — As an audit operator, I want a parent audit to evaluate
  its own closure against the children's status as it was when the audit
  started, so an otherwise-complete parent is reported `Yes` even if a child
  is re-screened as a side effect.
- **Release manager** — As a release manager, I want a parent audit to never
  demote a completed/`in_review` child unless that child was deliberately,
  independently audited as not-ready, so a parent run cannot silently push
  completed work back into the actionable queue and cascade `blocked` states
  through the dependency chain.
- **Maintainer** — As a maintainer, I want verdicts driven only by
  unverifiable/historical or out-of-manifest ACs to be distinguishable from
  genuine code gaps, so a read-only re-audit does not downgrade an
  already-reviewed child.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Snapshot/exception semantics:** A children snapshot is taken at
   parent-audit start, and the parent's closure decision exempts every child
   that was in `in_review`/`done` (or otherwise exempt) at that point — even
   if the child's stage changed during the parent run. A parent whose own ACs
   are all `met`/`adjusted` is not blocked by children that were exempt at
   audit start.
2. **No side-effect demotion:** A child audit that is triggered as a side
   effect of a parent audit (the `--audit-children` cascade or the
   content-changed auto re-screen) does not change the child's lifecycle
   (`status`/`stage`) when the child was `in_review`/`done` before the parent
   run. Only a child explicitly and independently audited as not-ready may be
   demoted.
3. **No regression to genuine blocking:** A child that is in a pre-review
   stage (`idea`, `intake_complete`, `plan_complete`) or that is independently
   audited and genuinely not-ready still blocks the parent's closure. The
   existing exemption rules and the parent-first pass-through are preserved.
4. **Verdict fidelity:** ACs that are unverifiable in a read-only audit
   (historical/execution-dependent properties, or verification files outside
   the child's file-scope manifest) do not silently become blocking `partial`
   verdicts that demote an otherwise-complete item; either they are handled by
   the snapshot/no-demotion fix or they carry a distinct non-blocking
   classification.
5. **Regression test:** An automated test pins acceptance criterion 1 and 2:
   a parent audit over an `in_review` child whose only failing AC is
   unverifiable yields parent `Ready to close: Yes` and leaves the child at
   `completed`/`in_review` (or, if the chosen approach preserves the child
   stage via snapshot instead, the test asserts the parent `Yes` and the
   pre-audit child stage).
6. **Documentation:** `skill/audit/SKILL.md` and
   `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` document the child-exemption snapshot
   / no-side-effect-demotion contract, including how `--audit-children` and
   the content-changed re-screen interact with it. All related documentation is
   updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any
   relevant wiki or docs site entries.
7. **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- The audit remains **read-only** except the authorized persistence and
  verdict-driven status lifecycle; the fix must not add new state mutations.
- Must not weaken genuine blocking: a truly not-ready, independently audited
  child must still block its parent.
- Must preserve the existing `in_review`/`done` exemption, `inherited_pass`
  pass-through, and content-fingerprint freshness/reuse semantics.
- Keep the change surgical; prefer extracting shared logic over duplicating
  stage/verdict logic between `_has_phase1_blocking_issues` and
  `_build_issue_json`.
- Any change to child lifecycle must be consistent between the markdown
  report path (`_assemble_issue_report`) and the JSON path
  (`_build_issue_json`).

## Existing state

- `_has_phase1_blocking_issues()` and `_build_issue_json()` exempt children
  whose **current** `stage` is `in_review` (plus `status=completed` +
  `stage=done`, deleted, and `inherited_pass`). The exemption is evaluated at
  report-assembly time, against whatever stage the child holds *after* the
  parent run.
- The `--audit-children` cascade auto-triggers
  `audit_runner.py issue <child> --force`; that child run applies its own
  terminal lifecycle (`_apply_terminal_lifecycle`): a genuine `No` verdict
  transitions the child to `open`/`plan_complete` (and `wl` dependency state
  can surface it as `blocked`). The parent then evaluates its exemption
  against the demoted child stage and blocks.
- In the default parent-first flow, children whose content-fingerprint
  changed are re-screened and their audits persisted via
  `_persist_child_audit()`, which does not itself change the child stage — so
  the observed demotion originates in the cascade re-audit path.
- Unverifiable ACs (e.g. "the tests fail for behavioural reasons *before*
  F3–F5 land", or a file outside the child's file-scope manifest) fall to
  `partial`, a blocking verdict, which drives the child `No` and the
  subsequent demotion.

## Desired change

Make a parent audit non-destructive to already-exempt children and evaluate
the parent's closure against the child-exemption status captured at audit
start. Candidate mechanisms (the implementer may choose any that satisfies all
ACs, or a combination):

- **Snapshot exempt children at audit start** and evaluate the parent's
  closure against the snapshot rather than the post-re-audit stages
  (satisfies AC1).
- **Preserve a child's prior terminal stage** when a cascade-triggered child
  audit's verdict is driven only by unverifiable / out-of-manifest ACs
  (satisfies AC2, AC4).
- **Make child re-audit opt-in** so the default parent audit never mutates
  child lifecycle (satisfies AC2, complements AC1).
- **Introduce a distinct `unverifiable` verdict** for
  historical/execution-dependent ACs so they do not silently become blocking
  `partial` (satisfies AC4).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — `_has_phase1_blocking_issues()`,
  `_build_issue_json()`, `_phase_children()` (cascade / auto-trigger),
  `_apply_terminal_lifecycle()`, `_child_content_changed()`,
  `_persist_child_audit()`, `_assemble_issue_report()`: snapshot exempt
  children at start; suppress side-effect demotion; keep markdown and JSON
  verdict paths consistent.
- `tests/test_audit_runner_review.py` — existing exemption/verdict unit tests
  (`test_child_audit_does_not_block_phase1_when_in_review`,
  `test_ready_false_when_child_audit_no`, etc.); add the regression test for
  AC5.
- `tests/test_audit_runner_core.py` — child inclusion / lifecycle tests
  (e.g. `test_completed_in_review_child_included_in_child_results`); extend
  for the snapshot/exemption behaviour.
- `skill/audit/SKILL.md` — Status Lifecycle + child-exemption documentation.
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — parent-first pass-through and
  `--audit-children` cascade documentation.
- `skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py` — only if the fix needs to suppress or
  gate a lifecycle transition for cascade-triggered child audits.

## Risks and mitigations

- **Over-broad exemption (regression risk):** snapshotting "exempt at start"
  could let a genuinely broken child block-free if the parent started while
  the child was still `in_review`. Mitigation: keep the existing pre-review
  and independent-audit blocking paths intact (AC3) and add explicit tests
  for the pre-review block.
- **Fix only patches the parent decision, not the child demotion:** the child
  still ends up `open`/`blocked`, leaving the release queue inconsistent.
  Mitigation: treat AC1 and AC2 as jointly required, not alternatives.
- **Two divergent verdict paths:** `_build_issue_json()` and
  `_assemble_issue_report()` could drift. Mitigation: extract shared
  exemption/verdict logic and test both paths.
- **Cascade never re-audits genuinely changed children:** if re-audit becomes

  `wl audit-show SA-0MUG0WFP8008WN63 --json`.

As a Pi extension maintainer, I want regression tests that inject a **stale
`ExtensionContext`** (after a session replacement/reload) into the
`proxy-compaction-bridge` and `proxy-sse-signals` extension logic, so a stale
ctx can never crash an unrelated run and the fix is proven red-before-green.

Parent: **SA-0MUEIOGT2005IR7F**. Covers parent AC2 (stale-ctx-safe extensions)
and AC4 (Node-side regression tests that fail against pre-fix code).

## Scope

- Add `node:test` coverage that injects a stale-ctx stub whose `ui` /
  `sessionManager` accessors **throw** the pi stale-ctx error, then assert the
  extension's handler/callback behaviour is a safe no-op / context passthrough
  rather than a throw.
- Follow the existing pure-module architecture: the guard/decision helper must
  live in the dependency-free JS core (`compaction-bridge.js`,
  `sse-signals.js`) so it is importable by `tests/unit/**/*.mjs` (node v22

# [IMPL] Harden proxy-compaction-bridge against stale ctx

## Goal

As a Pi extension maintainer, I want `proxy-compaction-bridge` to no-op when
the captured `ctx` has been invalidated by a session replacement, so its
handlers never throw `This extension ctx is stale ...` and never crash or
degrade an unrelated run.

Parent: **SA-0MUEIOGT2005IR7F**. Covers parent AC2 and part of AC5.

## Scope

- `pi-client/proxy-compaction-bridge/index.ts`: both the
  `after_provider_response` and `context` handlers call
  `ctx.sessionManager.getSessionId()` — a stale ctx throws.
- Move the session-id resolution into a stale-safe helper in the dependency-free
  core `compaction-bridge.js` (e.g. `safeSessionId(ctx)` returning `null` when
  access throws). The adapter must:
  - `after_provider_response`: no-op when the session id cannot be resolved.
  - `context`: return `undefined` (pass through messages unchanged) when the
    session id cannot be resolved.
- Never let a stale-ctx throw escape a handler; never mutate dispatch on an
  unknown session.
- Update `docs/dev/proxy-compaction-bridge.md` to document the stale-ctx
  fail-safe behaviour.
- Preserve the compaction-bridge wire contract (LP-0MTYGZ1DI0004QP8) and the
  existing dispatch reshape semantics exactly.

## Acceptance Criteria

- With a stale-ctx stub, both handlers do not throw; `context` returns
   `undefined` (passthrough) and `after_provider_response` performs no state
   update.
- With a live ctx, behaviour is byte-for-byte unchanged (existing
   compaction/reshape tests continue to pass, wire contract intact).
- `docs/dev/proxy-compaction-bridge.md` documents the stale-ctx fail-safe
   path and this work item.
- The stale-ctx regression tests added by the test item pass (green).

## Minimal Implementation

- Add `safeSessionId(ctx)` (try/catch around `ctx.sessionManager.getSessionId()`)
  to `compaction-bridge.js` and export it.

- Add the docs paragraph.

- Stale-safe `proxy-compaction-bridge` handlers.
- Documented fail-safe behaviour.

## Goal

As a Pi extension maintainer, I want `proxy-sse-signals` to no-op when its
captured UI handle (`statusUi`) belongs to an invalidated ctx, so a
session-replacement cannot make its async capturing-fetch callback throw and

## Problem statement

The audit runner's automatic full-suite execution path (F3, SA-0MSTN5KRF0097TVP) calls run_cached(..., force=True) from skill/test_cache.py directly instead of going through skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py. run_cached does not acquire the shared test semaphore (TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY / TEST_LOCK_TIMEOUT) that run_tests.py uses (SA-0MTG5U75A001F1RG). # Test groups for targeted, stage-aware testing

**Discovered-from:** SA-0MU32TCFM003B78I (R2 JSON-contract hardening). Its targeted-scope landing was blocked because the full suite now takes ~42 minutes and exceeds `.pi/test-config.json` `timeoutPerCommand=1500`.

## Problem

`run_tests.py` supports `--scope full|changed` and `--type`, but:

- `implement.py finish` falls back to the **full** suite whenever changed-scope selection is unavailable, and there is no way to run a small, meaningful group;
- the full suite now takes ~40+ minutes and exceeds the configured per-command timeout, so the finish gate times out during normal implementation;
- "changed" scope is file-based but not group-aware (an audit change should run the audit group, not the whole suite).

## Users

- **AI agents (implement phase)**: need a fast, targeted test run after each code change to iterate quickly without hitting the 1500s timeout.
- **CI system**: needs a predictable gate strategy — small groups for PR/iteration, full suite for release.
- **Producers/reviewers**: need confidence that the correct tests ran for a given change (an audit change should not be validated by running every test in the repo).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `.pi/test-config.json` (or the project test extension) defines named test groups with their commands, and the schema is documented in `docs/dev/`.
2. `run_tests.py --group <name>` runs exactly that group; `--list-groups` lists the available groups.
3. A changed-file → group selector maps touched paths to the smallest sufficient group (e.g. `skill/audit/**` → `audit`), with a documented fallback to `full` when selection is uncertain.
4. `implement.py finish` runs the selected targeted group during iteration (build → test) so iteration no longer triggers a full-suite run, while the full group remains the gate before `dev`/`main`.
5. Per-group runtime is measured, and either the full-suite timeout is right-sized or the full group is made fast enough that `finish` completes within the configured timeout.
6. Tests cover group resolution, changed-file selection, and the fallback to `full`.
7. Full project test suite passes.

## Constraints

- UK English.
- Backwards compatible: existing `--scope full|changed` behaviour and cache keys are preserved.
- No project-specific commands hard-coded in shared tooling — groups live in project config.
- Reuse the existing test cache; groups must not create stale or mismatched cache entries.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` — Add `--group` and `--list-groups` arguments; new group resolution logic
- `skill/test_cache.py` — Ensure cache keys are compatible with group-scoped runs
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — Wire in the targeted group selector during `finish`
- `.pi/test-config.json` — Define named groups and path→group mapping rules
- `docs/dev/` — Document the new test group schema and selector behaviour

## Risks & Assumptions

### Risks

1. **Scope creep** — Risk that the work expands to also refactor the entire `run_tests.py` test-type system. Mitigation: keep groups orthogonal to types; groups are a new dimension, not a replacement.
2. **Cache key collisions** — A group-scoped run could produce a cache entry that is later mistaken for a full-suite entry (or vice versa). Mitigation: include group name in the cache key.
3. **Changed-file ambiguity** — A single commit touching both audit and test-skill code would match multiple groups. Mitigation: select the smallest sufficient group, or require the user to disambiguate with `--group`.
4. **Full-suite timeout** — If the full suite remains >1500s, the release gate still times out. Mitigation: AC5 explicitly measures and either right-sizes the timeout or speeds up the full group.

### Assumptions

- The project's test suite is split across pytest and node — group definitions should account for both.
- The test extension mechanism (`skills_extensions/test/extension.json`) is the preferred mechanism for per-project group definitions.
- `implement.py` currently uses a hard-coded subset of logic to select changed tests; the group selector should reuse or refactor that logic rather than duplicating it.
- The default test group (when no `--group` is specified and changed-file selection is not available) is `full`, preserving existing behaviour.

## Related work

- **SA-0MU32TCFM003B78I** (R2: Harden the audit JSON contract) — This work item was discovered because R2's landing was blocked by the full-suite timeout.
- **SA-0MU2PXILZ000RPR1** — Open item about raising `timeoutPerCommand`; this work item may obviate the need for that if groups provide sufficient iteration speed.
- **SA-0MT6CENPW004V2JN** — The existing changed-file → test selector that `implement.py` uses; the group selector should build on this.
- **SA-0MUG30J5F001L57H** — `run_tests.py` live-repo snapshot guard; group-scoped runs should be compatible.
data.title: Provide targeted test groups for stage-aware testing (avoid full-suite Phase 2 timeouts)

# Ship close step falsely refuses to close released items whose descendants are already `stage=done`

Refiled from ContextHub (originally WL-0MUJKDX93000BJB4, now deleted there) — the defect is in SorraAgents' ship skill (`skill/ship/scripts/run-release.js`), so it is tracked here.

Discovered while investigating why the ContextHub v1.0.16 release auto-closed **0 of 14** released `in_review` items.

## Problem

`closeWorkItemsAfterRelease()` in `skill/ship/scripts/run-release.js` refuses to `wl close --force <parent>` whenever **any** descendant is not itself in the close-candidate set. The candidate set is built from `getCandidateItems()` (`skill/ship/scripts/check-audit-gate.js`), which returns **only** `stage: in_review` items.

Descendants already terminal (`stage: done`) are therefore *not* candidates, so they are classified as "collateral" and the parent close is refused — even though a done child needs no action and re-affirming it is harmless.

## Evidence (ContextHub v1.0.16)

11 parents refused; their combined descendants classified:

- **29 already `stage: done`** → false-positive collateral (the defect)
- **1 `stage: in_review` with `needsProducerReview=true`** → legitimately skipped, but also counted as collateral
- **18 open/blocked non-terminal** (`intake_complete`/`plan_complete`) → refusal is correct (force-close must not sweep unfinished work)

Per parent:

| Parent (ContextHub WL id) | done children | non-terminal children | Refusal valid? |
|---|---|---|---|

## Summary

The audit runner's Phase 2 FILE SCOPE manifest omits the audited item's **committed** touched files whenever the working tree is clean, causing false "outside the manifest" / `unmet` verdicts for criteria whose implementation and tests live in those committed files.

Discovered during the audit of SA-0MUIA3OE40001QJX (log: `~/.audit_debug/SorraAgents/audit_run_SA-0MUIA3OE40001QJX_20260927T095408.log`).

## Evidence

- The audit of SA-0MUIA3OE40001QJX returned `Ready to close: No` with parent AC1 `partial`, AC2 `unmet`, AC3 `unmet` — each justified by wording such as "`test_cache._default_runner`/`run_tests.py` are outside the provided manifest" and "test_cache is outside the manifest so its runner cannot be verified".
- The item's implementation commit `a83ada6a` changed 14 files (`git show --stat a83ada6a`): `.githooks/pre-push`, `docs/dev/test-isolation.md`, `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`, `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_concurrency.py`, `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py`, `skill/shared/tests/test_git_sandbox.py`, `skill/ship/SKILL.md`, `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py`, `skill/test_cache.py`, `skill/test_runner.py`, `tests/test_implement_sys_path_resolution.py`, `tests/test_repository_override_isolation.py`, `tests/test_run_tests_cache.py`.
- `git log --all --fixed-strings --grep=SA-0MUIA3OE40001QJX --name-only` returns all of those files, so the data is available — the manifest simply did not use it.
- The manifest actually used contained only `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` and `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_core.py`; the latter is **not** in `a83ada6a`.
- The working tree was clean at audit time (`git status --porcelain` showed only `.worklog/scheduled-prompts.json`).

## Root cause

`_build_file_scope_manifest()` (`skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py:4351`) builds the manifest's file list from:

1. the description's Key Files (`_extract_key_files`);
2. `_git_changed_files()` (`audit_runner.py:4210`) — `git diff --name-only HEAD` plus `git status --porcelain=v1`, i.e. **working-tree / untracked changes only**;
3. Phase 1 evidence `file:line` refs;
4. a lightweight repo index.

It does **not** use `_resolve_touched_files()` (`audit_runner.py:1476`), which already resolves the union of (a) files in commits referencing the item id (`git log --all --fixed-strings --grep=<id> --name-only`), (b) comment-recorded commit hashes, and (c) Key Files — the correct source for a fully-committed item on a clean checkout.

Consequently, when an item's work is committed and the tree is clean (the normal post-implementation state), `_git_changed_files()` contributes nothing and the manifest collapses to the Phase 1 evidence refs + repo index. The `_validate_file_scope_manifest()` fail-fast guard (`audit_runner.py:1231`) does not abort because the manifest does reference *some* item-repo file, even though it omits the item's actual touched files.

## Desired behaviour

`_build_file_scope_manifest()` must include the audited item's committed touched files (via `_resolve_touched_files()`), so a clean checkout still yields a manifest covering the item's real changes. The fail-fast scope validation must not accept a manifest that references the item repo but omits the item's touched files.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `_build_file_scope_manifest()` includes the audited item's committed touched files (reuse `_resolve_touched_files()`), in addition to the working-tree diff, Key Files, Phase 1 refs, and repo index.
- [ ] Regression test: with a clean working tree and a committed commit whose message references the item id, the built manifest contains that commit's changed files.
- [ ] A scope-validation regression test asserts that a manifest which references the item repo but omits the item's touched files is rejected (or is impossible to build).
- [ ] Re-auditing SA-0MUIA3OE40001QJX after this fix no longer reports its ACs as "outside the manifest" solely because the item's files are committed rather than uncommitted.
- [ ] Full suite green.

## Key Files (predicted)

- skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py — `_build_file_scope_manifest`, `_git_changed_files`, `_resolve_touched_files`, `_validate_file_scope_manifest`
- skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_core.py

## Related work

- discovered-from:SA-0MUIA3OE40001QJX — the audit whose false-negative verdicts surfaced this defect.
- Blocks the accurate re-audit/closure of SA-0MUIA3OE40001QJX (dependency edge recorded).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

### Q1 (RESOLVED) — Does AC3 require hardening `_validate_file_scope_manifest()`, or is the "impossible to build" regression test sufficient? (raised by Map, session `herdr-1790545473-1902849-18949`)
- **Context:** AC3 says a manifest that references the item repo but omits the item's touched files must be "rejected (or is impossible to build)". The Desired-behaviour section separately states the fail-fast scope validation "must not accept a manifest that references the item repo but omits the item's touched files", which reads as a validator-hardening requirement.
- **Preferred option (recommended):** harden `_validate_file_scope_manifest()` with an optional `touched_files` argument: when a non-empty touched set is resolvable and none of its paths appear in the manifest, return a scope error; when the set is `None`/empty, fail open (preserves current behaviour for mono-repo/unknown cases). Plan child SA-0MUKCOW1I001MJ7O covers this; the regression test is delivered either way.
- **Alternative A:** satisfy AC3 solely with the "impossible to build" regression test (no validator change).
- **Answer:** ACCEPTED (producer, 2026-09-27): **harden**. `_validate_file_scope_manifest()` gains an optional `touched_files` argument that returns a scope error when a non-empty resolved touched set has no path in the manifest, and fails open when the set is `None`/empty. Delivered by SA-0MUKCOW1I001MJ7O; the regression test is still required.

### Q2 (RESOLVED) — The item's `effort`/`risk` fields are lowercase ("medium"/"medium"), so the plan-approval gate's documented Medium-effort trigger did not fire. (raised by Map, session `herdr-1790545473-1902849-18949`)
- **Context:** `should_request_plan_approval()` compares `effort` case-sensitively against `{"Medium", "Large", "Extra Large"}`. `wl show` reports this item's values as `"medium"`/`"medium"` (other items, e.g. SA-0MUIA3OE40001QJX, use `"Medium"`/`"Severe"`). `plan_helpers.py plan-approval-gate` therefore returned `request_approval: false`, skipping the human checkpoint the skill documents for Medium effort.
- **Preferred option (recommended):** correct the item's `effort`/`risk` to canonical capitalised values and, if plan sign-off is wanted, review the child breakdown before implementation. (Making the gate case-insensitive is a separate change, out of scope here.)
- **Alternative A:** accept the gate result as-is and proceed without a producer approval pause (what this run did).
- **Answer:** ACCEPTED (producer, 2026-09-27): **correct**. The item's `effort`/`risk` were set to the canonical capitalised values (`Medium`/`Medium`) via `wl update`. With the corrected data, `plan-approval-gate` returns `request_approval: true` ("its effort is Medium scale"), so the plan is surfaced to the producer for sign-off before implementation.

### Q3 (OPEN QUESTION) — `extract_acceptance_criteria()` only exits the AC section on an `##` heading, so an H1-headed description makes the AC-coverage review treat Key Files / Related-work bullets as ACs and recommend `stop`. (raised by Map, session `herdr-1790545473-1902849-18949`)
- **Context:** `skill/shared/tree_coverage.py::extract_acceptance_criteria` detects the AC header with `^#+\s+Acceptance\s+Criteria` but breaks only on `^##\s+`. This plan normalised this item's and its children's headings to `##` (conformant with the AGENTS.md `## Acceptance Criteria` convention) so coverage parses correctly. Tracked as discovered-from work item SA-0MUKCQ4TL0075WZJ.
- **Preferred option (recommended):** reaffirm the H2 convention for descriptions and make the extractor break on any heading level 1–6 for robustness.
- **Answer:** _OPEN — informational; no plan decision depends on it._

### Plan approval (2026-09-27)

- **Decision:** APPROVED — producer replied "LGTM" to the four-child, test-first plan (SA-0MUKCOQI10095463 → SA-0MUKCOUXN001VH47 → SA-0MUKCOW1I001MJ7O → SA-0MUKCOX3T0057ES6). The plan-approval gate (Medium effort) is satisfied; `needsProducerReview` is cleared and the plan is ready for implementation.
data.title: Audit FILE SCOPE manifest omits a clean tree's committed touched files, causing false out-of-scope verdicts
